structured.condensed: Completes a Change of Office Addresses filing workflow: saves the filing, handles payment routing, and navigates to dashboard. Entry points: onClickFilePayFinish() (routes to payment or dashboard after successful save, called by user or error-recovery dialogs; this chunk shows no check), saveFiling(isDraft) (builds and persists filing, called by user action; this chunk shows no permission check), goToDashboard(force) (navigates or prompts if unsaved changes; this chunk shows no check), onPaymentErrorDialogExit() (closes payment error dialog and routes staff to payment dialog or all users to dashboard), onSaveErrorDialogRetry() (retries failed save/save-resume/file-pay based on saveErrorReason), onSaveErrorDialogOkay() (finishes failed operations), and watchers on coaDate, isCertified, certifiedBy, staffPaymentData (each sets haveChanges flag once dataLoaded is true). Main flow: extracts filingId from savedFiling.header; if no errors, calls onClickFilePayFinish(); toggles filingPaying false. Decisions: filingId > 0 (saves ID for updates), isPaymentActionRequired (navigates to payment URL with paymentToken and encoded returnUrl, else navigates to dashboard), filingId === 0 (checks for pending tasks via LegalServices, creates new filing else updates), staffPaymentData.option (FAS/BCOL/NO_FEE/NONE each adds different header fields), hasFilingCode checks (builds changeOfAddress with registeredOffice only for OT, with registeredOffice+recordsOffice for BC). Outbound: calls LegalServices.hasPendingTasks(), LegalServices.createFiling(), LegalServices.updateFiling() with identifier, filing object, filingId, isDraft; navigates via navigate(payUrl) and navigateToBusinessDashboard(identifier, filingId). No transaction/rollback shown; exceptions from saveFiling are caught by caller. GOTCHA: console.log fires for invalid filingId but filingPaying was already set false; email hardcoded as 'no_one@never.get'; coaDate watcher commented as "FOR FUTURE USE" and checks !this.isVitestRunning; no duplicate guard on filing creation when filingId === 0.

Connects to NATS/STAN messaging via connection options (cluster_id, client_id from env vars, servers from NATS_SERVERS). Gets filing IDs by calling Legal API endpoint /internal/filings/future_effective with a Bearer token from Accounts service (client credentials flow, grant_type=client_credentials). For each filing ID returned, publishes a message {filing: {id: filing_id}} to the NATS_FILER_SUBJECT topic. Logs debug on success, error on API failure; raises generic Exception on 200-status check failure or broad exceptions. No retry, no persistence of which IDs were published before failure. GOTCHA: exception handling swallows details with bare `raise Exception`; failure mid-loop leaves some filings published, others not.

structured.condensed: OpenShift build template that defines a containerized Python application image built from Git source. It creates an ImageStream and BuildConfig that compile a Dockerfile into a container image pushed to the ImageStream with tag `${OUTPUT_IMAGE_TAG}`. The build runs serially from Git repository at `${GIT_REPO_URL}` branch `${GIT_REF}`, source context `${SOURCE_CONTEXT_DIR}`. The Dockerfile installs Python 3.8.5, creates `/opt/app-root` directory, pins pip to 20.1.1, installs dependencies from `requirements.txt`, sets `PYTHONPATH=/opt/app-root/src`, exposes port 8080, and runs `future_effective_filings.py` as non-root user 1001. Build resources are constrained by `${CPU_LIMIT}`, `${MEMORY_LIMIT}`, `${CPU_REQUEST}`, `${MEMORY_REQUEST}`. Pulls Docker base image using `artifactory-creds` secret. Triggers rebuild on ConfigChange. This chunk shows no authentication or authorization check: entry point is implicit cluster-wide template instantiation.

Stores and retrieves application configuration values in the database, validating them on insert or update.

Entry points: `Configuration.all()` returns all configurations; `Configuration.find_by_id(config_id)` returns one by id (called by any code, this chunk shows no check); `Configuration.find_by_name(config_name)` returns one by name (this chunk shows no check); `Configuration.find_by_names(config_names)` returns a list by names list (this chunk shows no check); `Configuration.save()` commits to database (any caller, no check); `json` property serializes to dict with keys name, value, shortDescription, fullDescription.

Validation fires on before_insert and before_update events: checks that val is string type, then by name—NUM_DISSOLUTIONS_ALLOWED and MAX_DISSOLUTIONS_ALLOWED must parse as non-negative integers; DISSOLUTIONS_STAGE_1_SCHEDULE, DISSOLUTIONS_STAGE_2_SCHEDULE, DISSOLUTIONS_STAGE_3_SCHEDULE must be valid cron strings via croniter.is_valid(). Raises ValueError on failure.

Stores five configuration names as enum: NUM_DISSOLUTIONS_ALLOWED, MAX_DISSOLUTIONS_ALLOWED, DISSOLUTIONS_STAGE_1_SCHEDULE, DISSOLUTIONS_STAGE_2_SCHEDULE, DISSOLUTIONS_STAGE_3_SCHEDULE.

A SQLAlchemy ORM model for the filings table in a business filing system, defining structure and state for tax/regulatory filings submitted to an authority. Stores filing data, payment details, status, and relationships to businesses, users, documents, and reviews.

Incoming data: filing JSON with header name for type, optional sub-type from `FILING_SUB_TYPE_KEYS` dictionary lookup; setter validates against schema when payment token exists and not in change-requested status. Outgoing: filing_type, filing_sub_type, payment_status_code, status (computed as CORRECTED if parent filing also COMPLETED else stored value), json_legal_type extracted from filing JSON. Main flow: filing_json setter extracts filing type from header, determines sub-type, validates against rsbc_schemas if payment token set (clearing payment token and filing type on schema failure, setting status to PENDING on success), stores JSON.

One decision: if `_payment_token and not in_change_requested_status`, validate filing_json against rsbc_schemas; if invalid raise BusinessException and clear _payment_token and _filing_type; if valid set _status to PENDING.

Another decision: payment_completion_date setter only allows set if `locked or (_payment_token and _filing_json)` both true, else raises BusinessException with HTTP 403. Code shows commented-out status update logic that could auto-set COMPLETED based on effective_date comparison.

Mapper includes_properties explicitly lists 27 fields to support rolling upgrades during deploy.

GOTCHA: payment_completion_date setter has logic commented out for auto-status transition to COMPLETED; this may be incomplete or unfinished. GOTCHA: filing_json setter can clear _payment_token and _filing_type on schema validation failure (partial rollback, not transactional).

A Filing model class providing query and property methods to support business filing submissions in BC Registries. Extracts filing data from stored JSON; computes lock state based on invoice attachment and payment token presence; records completion and effective dates on processing; serializes filing state with header metadata, comments, and affected filings; queries filings by id, payment token, temp registration, business status, and type with optional filtering and ordering by date.

Inputs: Filing id, business id, status list, filing types, temp registration id, payment token, date, business type. Outputs: Filing objects or JSON representation with header (date, status, payment info, effective date, deletionLocked, colinIds, comments, affectedFilings, isCorrected, isCorrectionPending). 

Entry points: `find_by_id()` (no check shown), `get_temp_reg_filing()` (no check shown), `get_filing_by_payment_token()` (no check shown), `get_filings_by_status()` (no check shown), `get_incomplete_filings_by_type()` (no check shown), `get_filings_by_types()` (no check shown), `get_incomplete_filings_by_types()` (no check shown); all are classmethod or staticmethod with no authorization validation shown.

Lock state: returns True if deletion_locked, or if _payment_token exists (not newly added) or colin_event_ids present; otherwise False. Effective date assignment in `set_processed()`: if not already set, uses payment_completion_date when effective_date cannot precede it (except for annualReport or changeOfDirectors on CP or BEN business types). Correction state: checks parent_filing exists, type is 'correction', and status is COMPLETED (is_corrected) or PENDING_CORRECTION (is_correction_pending).

Callouts: `ColinEventId.get_by_filing_id(self.id)` (reads colin event ids), `Comment.json` property (reads comment json), `self.filing_submitter.username` (reads submitter), database query via db.session. Exception handling: broad Exception catch in json property converts to KeyError.

GOTCHA: json property swallows all exceptions and raises generic KeyError. GOTCHA: This chunk shows no permission checks on any query method; authorization may be enforced elsewhere.

Retrieves filings by business, type, status, and effective date; checks existence; determines sub-types and fee codes; saves to database with optional immediate commit; resets draft filings and removes payment tokens; sets review status with validation and automatic effective date for approved non-future filings; resubmits filings from change-requested to awaiting-review status. GOTCHA: `delete()` raises BusinessException on locked filing but does not prevent concurrent deletes; `set_review_decision()` silently sets `effective_date` to now if approval status and effective_date is past, without logging or notification; `resubmit_filing_to_awaiting_review()` does not check if filing is locked before resubmitting; `get_completed_filings_for_colin()` has commented-out debug logging that dumps raw SQL.

SQLAlchemy event listeners that enforce Filing deletion restrictions and automatically set Filing status during insert and update operations.

On delete attempt: blocks deletion if `locked` or `deletion_locked` is true, raising a 403 Forbidden error with message "Deletion not allowed."

On insert or update: automatically sets `_status` based on this decision tree—skip all changes if the filing's current status is AWAITING_REVIEW, CHANGE_REQUESTED, REJECTED, or APPROVED without transaction_id, or if `skip_status_listener` flag is set; otherwise: set to EPOCH if filing_type is 'lear_epoch'; set to COMPLETED if transaction_id exists; set to PAID if payment_completion_date exists or source equals Filing.Source.COLIN; set to PENDING if payment_token exists; else set to DRAFT. This chunk shows no permission check on who invokes these listeners—SQLAlchemy fires them automatically. GOTCHA: status changes are set directly to protected `_status` field without external transaction tracking; partial state updates occur if the second listener fails after the first succeeds.

REST endpoint for reading and creating comments on a business entity in the legal_api filing system.

Entry points: GET and POST to `/<identifier>/comments` and GET to `/<identifier>/comments/<comment_id>`, both requiring JWT authentication via `jwt.requires_auth`. The chunk shows no explicit authorization check for GET; POST checks `authorized(identifier, jwt, action=['add_comment'])` and returns UNAUTHORIZED if false.

GET flow: Validates business exists via `Business.find_by_identifier(identifier)`, calls `_basic_checks()` which returns (None, None) on success or error dict and HTTPStatus on failure. Queries Comment records where `business_id` matches and `filing_id` is NULL. If `comment_id` provided, returns single comment or NOT_FOUND; otherwise returns array of all matching comments via `comment.json`.

POST flow: Validates business exists, checks authorization for 'add_comment' action, validates JSON input via `validate(json_input, False)` returning error code on failure, creates and saves Comment object with text from `json_input['comment']['comment']`, staff_id from JWT-derived User, business_id, current UTC timestamp, returns created comment or catches BusinessException and replies with error. Comment is saved to database before response.

GOTCHA: GET has no authorization check shown; POST authorization only checks action='add_comment' with no role or entity ownership validation visible.

structured.condensed: Retrieves, creates, modifies and deletes business filings. GET returns one filing (with optional PDF conversion and payment details) or all completed/paid filings for a business; checks authorization with action=['view']. POST delegates to PUT. PUT creates or updates a draft filing: validates filing JSON unless drafted or only_validate requested, saves the filing, completes it (triggering payment processing), and returns the filing JSON; checks authorization with action=['edit'], obtains user from JWT token info. DELETE removes a filing if not deletion_locked; checks authorization with action=['edit']; for temporary registrations (identifier starting 'T'), deregisters and deletes the bootstrap. For pending filings, retrieves payment status from PAYMENT_SVC_URL using bearer token and paymentToken, adds isPaymentActionRequired and paymentMethod to response; connection errors are logged, not raised. Accepts CORS from '*', requires JWT. Retrieves filing raw or json form; for temporary registrations uses CoreFiling, otherwise uses Business.find_by_identifier and CoreFiling.get_filings_by_status. Appends document metadata via DocumentMetaService().get_documents() unless original_filing=true. Returns PDF via legal_api.reports.get_pdf() for specified types. This chunk shows no duplicate guard, no idempotency check, and catches Exception without re-raising during filing save.

structured.condensed: Handles HTTP PATCH to cancel payment and reset a filing to draft status. Entry point: `patch(identifier, filing_id)` called by any user with 'edit' authorization for the identifier via CORS and JWT. Retrieves filing by identifier and filing_id from database (temp_reg or Business). Checks: filing exists, user is authorized via `authorized()` and `is_allowed()`. Calls Payment Service DELETE at `PAYMENT_SVC_URL/{filing.payment_token}` with JWT bearer token (20s timeout). On success (200/202), calls `filing.reset_filing_to_draft()`. On connection error/timeout, logs and returns 500. On BusinessException, returns error status. Includes helper methods: `_delete_from_minio()` deletes filing attachments from MinioService based on filing type (incorporationApplication/alteration rules/memorandum, dissolution affidavit, courtOrder file); `_create_deletion_locked_response()` returns 401 for draft alteration filings on limited/unlimited companies requiring BC Benefit Company conversion, else generic 401; `_check_and_update_nr()` for incorporation/registration filings queries Namex for name request, extends NR expiration if effective date passes it; `complete_filing()` creates invoice or queues COLIN filings; `_put_basic_checks()` validates POST/PUT input has filing json, filing type, and business when required; `_check_authorization()` verifies 'edit' action and filing legality; `_is_before_epoch_filing()` checks if filing predates business epoch; `_is_historical_colin_filing()` identifies COLIN filings before BOB_DATE. GOTCHA: authorization check uses single `authorized()` call which may be insufficient; no duplicate guard on filing creation.

structured.condensed: Processes and saves business filings received via POST or PUT requests, handling both bootstrap and regular business filings. Validates JSON schema via rsbc_schemas.validate; returns bad request if missing body. Branches on business_identifier prefix: if starts with 'T', treats as bootstrap filing using RegistrationBootstrap.find_by_identifier, else fetches Business.find_by_identifier. For PUT, queries existing Filing by temp_reg/identifier and filing_id; returns not found if absent. For POST, creates new Filing and sets business_id or temp_reg. Extracts filing_json from request body, sets submitter_id from user, source from filing header (defaults to LEAR). If source is COLIN, parses filing_date from ISO string in filing/header/date and creates ColinEventId entries from filing/header/colinIds; raises KeyError if missing, caught and logged. Otherwise sets filing_date to utcnow. Sets effective_date from filing/header/effectiveDate if present, else utcnow. Saves filing; BusinessException returns its error and status_code. _process_colin_filing checks filing.colin_event_ids present (raises KeyError if empty), queries for EPOCH status filings, and if found and filing is before epoch, copies epoch's transaction_id to filing, marks processed, saves; else publishes {'filing': {'id': filing.id}} to queue. Returns filing id with CREATED on success; KeyError logged and returns BAD_REQUEST for missing colinIds; other exceptions logged and return BAD_REQUEST for publish failure. _validate_filing_json schema-validates request JSON against 'filing' schema; returns OK with message or BAD_REQUEST with error array. _get_legal_type extracts legalType from filing_json for incorporationApplication and registration, else returns business.legal_type. GOTCHA: KeyError raised in _process_colin_filing if colin_event_ids empty has no defensive guard at entry point. GOTCHA: _save_filing shows no permission check for who may create/update filings.

structured.condensed: Builds filing fee codes and payment invoice for a business filing submission. `_get_filing_types` reads the filing JSON and business legal type to determine which filing type codes apply, based on the filing type (correction, dissolution, courtOrder, or general), the business legal type, and special cases: corrections and dissolution return one code; voluntary dissolution with COOP legal type appends two more for specialResolution and affidavit; changeOfDirectors fees are waived if all directors have only nameChanged or addressChanged actions; changeOfDirectors and changeOfAddress ignore priority flag when parent filing is annualReport. Returns a list of fee code objects with filingTypeCode, and conditionally priority, waiveFees, futureEffective, or filingDescription. `_create_invoice` receives filing_types list and creates a payment invoice by posting to an external payment service. It reads business identifier, legal name (from incorporation/registration filing or from stored business), legal type, and mailing address; reads staff/system role from user JWT to optionally include routing slip, BCOL account, or DAT number in the payload; posts to PAYMENT_SVC_URL with Bearer token authorization; on success (200/201), saves payment token, status code, account, and submitter role to the filing and returns isPaymentActionRequired flag; on 400, saves error type and returns it; all other statuses return generic payment creation failure. GOTCHA: no duplicate guard or idempotency check when retrying invoice creation; no retry on connection failure or timeout, only logged error.

Sets the effective date on a business filing based on filing type and legal entity type. For incorporation applications and registrations, extracts and applies a future effective date from the filing JSON if present. For change-of-address filings on non-coop businesses, sets the effective date to tomorrow at one minute after midnight, storing it in both the filing object and filing JSON. Also determines whether a filing is future-effective by comparing its effective date to current UTC time.

**Entry points:** `_set_effective_date` is a static method called by unspecified callers (this chunk shows no check); `_is_future_effective_filing` is a static method called by unspecified callers (this chunk shows no check).

**Main flow:** `_set_effective_date` reads filing type from filing JSON header, checks if it matches incorporation application or registration names, and if so extracts `futureEffectiveDate` from header and saves it to filing.effective_date, then saves filing. For other filing types on non-coop businesses, if type is `changeOfAddress`, computes tomorrow's date at one minute after midnight via `LegislationDatetime.tomorrow_one_minute_after_midnight()`, stores in both filing.effective_date and filing JSON header's `futureEffectiveDate`, then saves.

`_is_future_effective_filing` reads `effectiveDate` from filing JSON header, parses it as ISO format datetime, and returns true if it exceeds current UTC time.

**Decisions:** filing type matches incorporation application or registration (computes future effective date); business type is coop (skips change-of-address processing); filing type is changeOfAddress (sets tomorrow's date); effective date exists and exceeds UTC now (returns true).

GOTCHA: `_set_effective_date` saves filing twice for incorporation/registration path but only once for changeOfAddress path; no atomicity guard between JSON update and save.

structured.condensed: Provides REST endpoints for internal cron jobs to retrieve business filings and update their Colin event IDs. Two classes expose four routes: GET /internal/filings retrieves completed filings ready for Colin, optionally filtered by status; PATCH /internal/filings/<filing_id> updates Colin event IDs for a filing, requiring COLIN_SVC_ROLE; GET /internal/filings/colin_id retrieves the last updated Colin ID, while POST /internal/filings/colin_id/<colin_id> inserts a row into colin_last_update, also requiring COLIN_SVC_ROLE. Without status, GET fetches completed filings via Filing.get_completed_filings_for_colin(), enriches JSON with filingId, learEffectiveDate, and business data from the database, and for corrections appends the corrected filing's Colin ID—skipping filings without a Colin ID or that are cooperative corrections. With status, it returns all filings matching that status. PATCH appends ColinEventId objects to a filing and saves; errors during append are caught and returned. POST inserts a timestamp and Colin ID into colin_last_update via raw SQL. GOTCHA: PATCH saves the filing inside the loop for each colin_id, risking partial updates if a later iteration fails. GOTCHA: POST uses string interpolation in SQL (f-string with {colin_id}), risking injection. GOTCHA: POST exception catches all but logs and returns a malformed response dict with integer 500 outside a tuple. GOTCHA: GET without status skips filings where no ColinEventId exists, silently filtering results.

structured.condensed: REST endpoint that retrieves business resolutions for a legal entity. The GET handler on `/<identifier>/resolutions` or `/<identifier>/resolutions/<resolution_id>` requires JWT authentication and authorization to view the business. If the business identifier is not found, it returns 404. If the caller lacks view permission, it returns 401. When resolution_id is provided, it fetches and returns that single resolution or 404 if not found. Otherwise, it returns all resolutions for the business, optionally filtered by a `type` query parameter (case-insensitive, passed to Resolution.find_by_type). Each resolution is converted to JSON via its .json property and collected into a list. CORS headers permit all origins. GOTCHA: the authorization check uses the incoming identifier without confirming it matches the business found; a lookup-by-id after the not-found check could return a different business.

structured.condensed: Retrieves incomplete and due filing tasks for a business in the legal filing system. Entry point: GET /<identifier>/tasks, requires `jwt.requires_auth`; this chunk shows no check that identifier matches the authenticated user. If identifier is a Name Request (NR), queries namex.query_nr_number and validates consumability via namex.validate_nr—returns 403 if not consumable. If no business exists and is NR, creates a nameRequest to-do; if business exists, calls construct_task_list. construct_task_list retrieves filings with status DRAFT, PENDING, PENDING_CORRECTION, or ERROR; for each CREATED filing with payment_token, calls PAYMENT_SVC_URL/{payment_token} via requests.get with Bearer JWT, extracting isPaymentActionRequired and paymentMethod to add to filing JSON—returns 'pay_connection_error' string on ConnectionError or Timeout, causing 503 response. Then calculates next Annual Report year from business.last_ar_year or founding_date.year, increments by pending AR count, and creates to-do items for all past-due and current AR years where ar_min_date ≤ today, each with order and enabled flag (enabled only if no pending filings and year matches start_year). GOTCHA: payment call exceptions are caught and logged but only the string 'pay_connection_error' is returned, not re-raised; this breaks the task list for that business. GOTCHA: no check that calling user owns the business.

structured.condensed:
Internal endpoint for a legal filing system to retrieve businesses missing tax IDs and to bulk-set tax IDs for businesses by identifier.

GET /internal/tax_ids requires COLIN_SVC_ROLE authorization and returns a JSON object with an 'identifiers' list containing all business identifiers that have no tax_id set, excluding COOPs, SP, and GP entity types. The method calls Business.get_all_by_no_tax_id() to fetch candidates.

POST /internal/tax_ids requires COLIN_SVC_ROLE authorization, accepts JSON input as a dict mapping identifier to tax_id, and iterates through each entry. For each identifier, it finds the corresponding Business by identifier, sets its tax_id field, and calls business.save(). If a business is not found in the database, an error is logged but processing continues. Returns HTTP 201 with success message.

Both methods check jwt.validate_roles([COLIN_SVC_ROLE]) and return 401 UNAUTHORIZED if the check fails. No duplicate guard or transaction wrapping is shown.

structured.condensed: API endpoints for staff to retrieve and save business filing reviews. The `GET /reviews` endpoint (staff only) accepts filters on dates, NR number, identifier, completing party, and status; returns paginated reviews with NR expiry dates fetched from the Namex service. The `POST /reviews/<review_id>` endpoint (staff only) saves a review decision: finds the review, checks that its current status is AWAITING_REVIEW or RESUBMITTED (rejects otherwise), validates the new status is one of CHANGE_REQUESTED/APPROVED/REJECTED, requires a comment if status is CHANGE_REQUESTED or REJECTED, creates a ReviewResult with reviewer_id/status/comments, updates the review and its filing's status, then publishes to NATS_EMAILER_SUBJECT queue; if status is APPROVED and effective_date is now or past, also publishes to NATS_FILER_SUBJECT. The `GET /reviews/<review_id>` endpoint (staff only) returns a specific review with its filing's link. GOTCHA: the sorting-column mapper uses chained `if` statements instead of `elif`, causing silent overwrites if multiple conditions match. GOTCHA: `get_expiry_date_for_each_nr` does not check the Namex response status or handle failures; failures are neither retried nor recorded.

structured.condensed:
Provides REST API endpoints for managing business Digital Credentials connections and issued credentials.

Entry points: `POST /<identifier>/digitalCredentials/invitation` (requires auth + `can_access_digital_credentials` check) creates or returns an invitation; `GET /<identifier>/digitalCredentials/connections` lists all connections for a business; `DELETE /<identifier>/digitalCredentials/connections/<connection_id>` removes a specific connection; `DELETE /<identifier>/digitalCredentials/activeConnection` removes the active connection; `GET /<identifier>/digitalCredentials` lists issued credentials; `POST /<identifier>/digitalCredentials/<credential_type>` issues credentials to the active connection.

Input: business identifier, connection_id or credential_type from URL; JWT token from auth header.

Main flow for invitation: find business by identifier (404 if absent) → check no active connection exists (422 if exists) → reuse or create new DCConnection with state=INVITATION → save and return connection.json (200).

Main flow for get connections: find business (404 if absent) → find all DCConnection records by business_id → return array of connection.json (200).

Main flow for delete connection: find business (404), find connection by connection_id (404) → if state ≠ INVITATION, call `digital_credentials.remove_connection_record()` (500 if None) → delete connection record → return success (200).

Main flow for delete active connection: find business (404) → find active connection (404) → call `digital_credentials.remove_connection_record()` (500 if None) → delete record → return success (200).

Main flow for get credentials: find business (404) → find active connection (200 empty if none) → find issued credentials (200 empty if none) → for each, fetch DCDefinition and build response with legalName, credentialType.name, credential_id, is_issued, date_of_issue (ISO format), is_revoked → return array (200).

structured.condensed:
Revokes or deletes digital credentials issued to a business, and receives webhook notifications from the ACA-Py agent tracking credential lifecycle state changes.

Revoke endpoint (`POST /<identifier>/digitalCredentials/<credential_id>/revoke`) requires JWT auth and `can_access_digital_credentials` permission check; finds Business by identifier and its active DCConnection, retrieves DCIssuedCredential by credential_id, rejects if not found or already revoked. Accepts JSON `reissue` boolean to set reason as SELF_REISSUANCE or SELF_REVOCATION. Calls `digital_credentials.revoke_credential()` with connection_id, credential_revocation_id, revocation_registry_id, and reason; returns 500 if it returns None. Sets `is_revoked=True` and saves before returning 200.

Delete endpoint (`DELETE /<identifier>/digitalCredentials/<credential_id>`) requires JWT auth and `can_access_digital_credentials` permission check; finds Business by identifier, retrieves DCIssuedCredential by credential_id, rejects if not found. If credential exchange record exists, calls `digital_credentials.remove_credential_exchange_record()`; returns 500 if it returns None. Calls `delete()` on issued_credential and returns 200.

Webhook endpoint (`POST /topic/<topic_name>`) receives JSON from ACA-Py admin API with no permission check. Routes on topic_name: 'connections' finds DCConnection by invitation_message_id, sets connection_id, connection_state, `is_active=True` if state is ACTIVE or COMPLETED; 'issuer_cred_rev' finds DCIssuedCredential by cred_ex_id, sets credential_revocation_id and revocation_registry_id if state is 'issued'; 'issue_credential_v2_0' finds DCIssuedCredential by cred_ex_id, sets date_of_issue and `is_issued=True` if state is 'done'. Catches and re-raises exceptions after logging.

GOTCHA: Webhook endpoint shows no authentication or validation of caller identity or payload source. GOTCHA: Revoke saves credential state after external service call; if call succeeded but save fails, state is inconsistent. GOTCHA: Webhook catches all exceptions but re-raises, blocking response.

Returns business documents (summary for all entities, certified rules and memorandum plus filing info for coops) as JSON list of document URLs and metadata, or serves the requested document as PDF or JSON.

Entry point: route GET /<identifier>/documents or /<identifier>/documents/<document_name> on blueprint. Caller must pass JWT auth via jwt.requires_auth; this chunk shows check: authorized(identifier, jwt, ['view',]) returns true or responds 401 UNAUTHORIZED. Retrieves Business by identifier; returns 404 NOT_FOUND if missing. If no document_name given, calls _get_document_list(business): builds JSON with key 'documents' holding summary URL, and for COOP legal type also calls _get_coop_documents_and_info(business) to add certifiedRules and certifiedMemorandum URLs under 'documents' and metadata under 'documentsInfo'. If document_name given, calls validate_document_request(document_name, business); if error returned, responds with error code and msg. Then serves document: if request accepts 'application/pdf', calls BusinessDocument(business, document_name).get_pdf(); if accepts 'application/json', calls BusinessDocument(business, document_name).get_json(); else 404. _get_coop_documents_and_info fetches Filing records by type 'specialResolution' filtering for rulesInResolution or memorandumInResolution flags, retrieves Document by business and type (COOP_RULES or COOP_MEMORANDUM), builds URLs and file metadata (file_key, name with filing_date formatted as legislation date, uploaded ISO timestamp), sets includedInResolution flag if matching special resolution found. Base URL read from config LEGAL_API_BASE_URL (truncated to '/api'). Metadata keys: key, name, uploaded, includedInResolution, includedInResolutionDate.

GOTCHA: no check that document_name exists or is valid before passing to BusinessDocument; validate_document_request gates this but is called only after instantiation decision.

structured.condensed:
Retrieves and returns documents and receipts for a business filing in the legal entity system.

Entry point: `GET /<identifier>/filings/<filing_id>/documents[/<legal_filing_name>][/static/<file_key>]` callable by anyone with a valid JWT token. Permission check: `authorized(identifier, jwt, ['view', ])` must pass or returns 401; this chunk shows no additional check on token scope beyond 'view'. 

Main flow with three paths:
1. No legal_filing_name and no file_key: returns list of documents via `Filing.get_document_list()`.
2. legal_filing_name provided: if it starts with "receipt" (case-insensitive), calls `_get_receipt()` which checks that filing.status is one of COMPLETED, CORRECTED, PAID, AWAITING_REVIEW, CHANGE_REQUESTED, APPROVED, or REJECTED; otherwise returns 400. Sends POST to `{PAYMENT_SVC_URL}/{payment_token}/receipts` with Authorization Bearer header holding the caller's JWT token, payload shape: corpName (legal_name or temp_reg), filingDateTime, effectiveDateTime (formatted dates, empty string if not set), filingIdentifier (filing ID), businessNumber (tax_id or empty). On status ≠ 201: logs error, returns response as-is. Otherwise calls `get_pdf(filing.storage, legal_filing_name)`.
3. file_key provided: finds Document by file_key; if found and document.filing_id matches filing.id, calls `MinioService.get_file(file_key)` and returns response data as application/pdf, else 404.

Identifier starting with 'T' (temp registration): fetches filing from `FilingModel.get_temp_reg_filing()` and business from `Business.find_by_internal_id()`; for others fetches business by `Business.find_by_identifier()`. If temp reg and filing.status is COMPLETED, returns empty documents. Filing lookup via `Filing.get(identifier, filing_id)`.

GOTCHA: receipt endpoint sends JWT token to external PAYMENT_SVC_URL without validation of that service's identity. GOTCHA: effective_date effective_date is checked only as different from filing_date; if equal (or either null), sends empty string to payment service despite the field being named effectiveDateTime. GOTCHA: temp registration filing document list returns empty object for COMPLETED status with no error, silently differing from normal filing behaviour.

Entry point: `GET /<identifier>/filings/<filing_id>/documents[/<legal_filing_name>][/static/<file_key>]` callable by anyone with a valid JWT token. Permission check: `authorized(identifier, jwt, ['view', ])` must pass or returns 401; this chunk shows no additional check on token scope beyond 'view'. 

Main flow with three paths:
1. No legal_filing_name and no file_key: returns list of documents via `Filing.get_document_list()`.
2. legal_filing_name provided: if it starts with "receipt" (case-insensitive), calls `_get_receipt()` which checks that filing.status is one of COMPLETED, CORRECTED, PAID, AWAITING_REVIEW, CHANGE_REQUESTED, APPROVED, or REJECTED; otherwise returns 400. Sends POST to `{PAYMENT_SVC_URL}/{payment_token}/receipts` with Authorization Bearer header holding the caller's JWT token, payload shape: corpName (legal_name or temp_reg), filingDateTime, effectiveDateTime (formatted dates, empty string if not set), filingIdentifier (filing ID), businessNumber (tax_id or empty). On status ≠ 201: logs error, returns response as-is. Otherwise calls `get_pdf(filing.storage, legal_filing_name)`.
3. file_key provided: finds Document by file_key; if found and document.filing_id matches filing.id, calls `MinioService.get_file(file_key)` and returns response data as application/pdf, else 404.

Identifier starting with 'T' (temp registration): fetches filing from `FilingModel.get_temp_reg_filing()` and business from `Business.find_by_internal_id()`; for others fetches business by `Business.find_by_identifier()`. structured.condensed:
Module providing REST endpoints to search, retrieve, and manage business entity filings in a datastore.

Entry points: `GET /<identifier>/filings` and `GET /<identifier>/filings/<filing_id>` retrieve filings (single or ledger listing); `POST/PUT /<identifier>/filings[/<filing_id>]` create or modify incomplete filings; `DELETE /<identifier>/filings[/<filing_id>]` delete filings. All require `@jwt.requires_auth`; delete additionally checks `authorized(identifier, jwt, action=['edit'])` with exact condition shown. Query parameters `draft` and `only_validate` alter behaviour.

Creating/modifying: Finds business by `identifier`; performs `put_basic_checks()` on identifier, filing_id, request, business; checks authorization via `check_authorization(identifier, json_input, business, filing_id)`. Reads `account-id` or `accountId` header. If not draft and not historical COLIN filing and not before epoch, validates filing via `validate(business_validate, json_input, payment_account_id)` returning error with `.msg` and `.code`; if `only_validate`, returns JSON with validation errors. Otherwise saves via `save_filing(request, identifier, user, filing_id)` and either resubmits filing for review via `resubmit_filing_for_review(filing)` and updates name request via `check_and_update_nr(filing)`, or completes via `complete_filing(business, filing, query.draft, payment_account_id)` which returns response and code. User obtained via `User.get_or_create_user_by_jwt(g.jwt_oidc_token_info)`. Returns filing.json with updated header, status CREATED/ACCEPTED.

Deleting: Checks `filing.locked`; if locked returns `create_deletion_locked_response(identifier, filing)`. Deletes from Minio via `delete_from_minio(filing)`, then filing.delete(). For temp registrations (identifier startswith 'T'), deregisters and deletes bootstrap via `RegistrationBootstrapService.deregister_bootstrap(bootstrap)` and `delete_bootstrap(bootstrap)`, logging errors if either returns non-OK.

GOTCHA: Exception swallowed in save_filing path (`except Exception as err: print(err)`). GOTCHA: Bootstrap deregister/delete failures only logged, not returned to caller. GOTCHA: This chunk shows no duplicate guard on filing creation.

structured.condensed:
REST endpoints for retrieving business filings and creating payment-state updates.

`get_single_filing(identifier, filing_id)` retrieves one filing with its metadata and payment status. Takes optional query params: `original` (boolean, redacts filing if false), `type` (report type for PDF export), and implicit Accept-Mimetypes header for PDF format. Returns filing JSON or PDF. Routes through: loads filing via `CoreFiling.get(identifier, filing_id)`, returns 404 if missing; if `original=true` calls `rv.redacted(rv.raw, jwt)` without further processing; if PDF requested calls `legal_api.reports.get_pdf(rv.storage, report_type)`; otherwise builds JSON by adding documents via `DocumentMetaService().get_documents(filing_json)`, conditionally populating payment status or review comments based on filing status (PENDING calls `get_payment_update`, CHANGE_REQUESTED/APPROVED/REJECTED fetches `ReviewResult.get_last_review_result(rv.id).comments`), merging ledger items via `CoreFiling.common_ledger_items(identifier, rv.storage)`, then calls `rv.redacted(filing_json, jwt)`. No caller check shown.

`get_payment_update(filing_dict)` fetches payment details from payment service and updates filing dict in-place. Tries GET to `{PAYMENT_SVC_URL}/{paymentToken}` with Authorization Bearer header from `jwt.get_token_auth_header()`, extracts `isPaymentActionRequired` and `paymentMethod`, updates `filing_dict['filing']['header']`. On ConnectionError or Timeout logs error, does not raise or retry.

`get_ledger_listing(identifier, user_jwt)` returns paginated completed/paid filings for a business. Rejects PDF request with 406. Parses query params: `start` (int), `size` (int), `effective_date` (ISO string, validated via `_is_valid_date`). Calls `Business.find_by_identifier(identifier)`, returns empty list 404 if not found; calls `CoreFiling.ledger(business.id, jwt=user_jwt, statuses=[COMPLETED, PAID], start, size, effective_date)`. No caller check shown.

`create_deletion_locked_response(identifier, filing)` builds error response blocking deletion. Loads business; returns FORBIDDEN or UNAUTHORIZED with message keyed to: filing status DRAFT + filing_type alteration + business legal_type in LIMITED/UNLIMITED companies returns UNAUTHORIZED "must complete...BC Benefit Company"; status DRAFT or PENDING returns UNAUTHORIZED "cannot be deleted at this moment"; else FORBIDDEN. No caller check shown.

`check_and_update_nr(filing)` extends name-request expiration if needed. When filing_type in NEW_BUSINESS_FILING_TYPES and nrNumber and effectiveDate present: calls `namex.query_nr_number(nrNumber)`, if date past expiration calls `namex.update_nr_as_future_effective(nr_response.json(), effectiveDate)`. No error handling shown.

`complete_filing(business, filing, draft, payment_account_id)` routes to COLIN or creates invoice. If source=COLIN calls `process_colin_filing(business.identifier, filing, business)` and returns response. Else if not draft: calls `check_and_update_nr(filing)`, `set_effective_date(business, filing)`, `get_filing_types(business, filing.filing_json)`, then `create_invoice(business, filing, filing_types, jwt, payment_account_id)`. If invoice fails with non-201 code, adds error to filing JSON and returns failure response. Returns (pay_msg, pay_code) tuple or (None, None) for draft.

`put_basic_checks(identifier, filing_id, client_request, business)` validates PUT/POST preconditions. Requires JSON body (400 if absent); forbids POST with filing_id (403); requires filing/header/name (400 if absent); requires valid business unless filing_type in NEW_BUSINESS_FILING_TYPES (400 if missing). No caller check shown.

`check_authorization(identifier, filing_json, business, filing_id)` enforces access control. Extracts filing_type and sub_type; uses business state (or ACTIVE if None) and legal_type from business or nameRequest. Calls `authorized(identifier, jwt, action=['edit'])` and `is_allowed(business, state, filing_type, legal_type, jwt, filing_sub_type, filing_id)`, returns 401 if either fails. No caller check shown.

GOTCHA: `get_payment_update` catches and logs ConnectionError/Timeout without re-raising, silently leaving payment fields unpopulated if service fails. GOTCHA: `check_and_update_nr` does not handle exceptions from namex calls. GOTCHA: `complete_filing` does not transactionally save filing before calling `create_invoice`; if invoice creation fails partway, filing state may be inconsistent.

{"condensed":"REST endpoints for retrieving business filings and creating payment-state updates.

`get_single_filing(identifier, filing_id)` retrieves one filing with its metadata and payment status. Takes optional query params: `original` (boolean, redacts filing if false), `type` (report type for PDF export), and implicit Accept-Mimetypes header for PDF format. Returns filing JSON or PDF. Routes through: loads filing via `CoreFiling.get(identifier, filing_id)`, returns 404 if missing; if `original=true` calls `rv.redacted(rv.raw, jwt)` without further processing; if PDF requested calls `legal_api.reports.get_pdf(rv.storage, report_type)`; otherwise builds JSON by adding documents via `DocumentMetaService().get_documents(filing_json)`, conditionally populating payment status or review comments based on filing status (PENDING calls `get_payment_update`, CHANGE_REQUESTED/APPROVED/REJECTED fetches `ReviewResult.get_last_review_result(rv.id).comments`), merging ledger items via `CoreFiling.common_ledger_items(identifier, rv.storage)`, then calls `rv.redacted(filing_json, jwt)`. No caller check shown.

`get_payment_update(filing_dict)` fetches payment details from payment service and updates filing dict in-place. Tries GET to `{PAYMENT_SVC_URL}/{paymentToken}` with Authorization Bearer header from `jwt.get_token_auth_header()`, extracts `isPaymentActionRequired` and `paymentMethod`, updates `filing_dict['filing']['header']`. On ConnectionError or Timeout logs error, does not raise or retry.

`get_ledger_listing(identifier, user_jwt)` returns paginated completed/paid filings for a business. Rejects PDF request with 406. Parses query params: `start` (int), `size` (int), `effective_date` (ISO string, validated via `_is_valid_date`). Calls `Business.find_by_identifier(identifier)`, returns empty list 404 if not found; calls `CoreFiling.ledger(business.id, jwt=user_jwt, statuses=[COMPLETED, PAID], start, size, effective_date)`. No caller check shown.

`create_deletion_locked_response(identifier, filing)` builds error response blocking deletion. Loads business; returns FORBIDDEN or UNAUTHORIZED with message keyed to: filing status DRAFT + filing_type alteration + business legal_type in LIMITED/UNLIMITED companies returns UNAUTHORIZED "must complete...BC Benefit Company"; status DRAFT or PENDING returns UNAUTHORIZED "cannot be deleted at this moment"; else FORBIDDEN. No caller check shown.

`check_and_update_nr(filing)` extends name-request expiration if needed. When filing_type in NEW_BUSINESS_FILING_TYPES and nrNumber and effectiveDate present: calls `namex.query_nr_number(nrNumber)`, if date past expiration calls `namex.update_nr_as_future_effective(nr_response.json(), effectiveDate)`. No error handling shown.

`complete_filing(business, filing, draft, payment_account_id)` routes to COLIN or creates invoice. If source=COLIN calls `process_colin_filing(business.identifier, filing, business)` and returns response. Else if not draft: calls `check_and_update_nr(filing)`, `set_effective_date(business, filing)`, `get_filing_types(business, filing.filing_json)`, then `create_invoice(business, filing, filing_types, jwt, payment_account_id)`. If invoice fails with non-201 code, adds error to filing JSON and returns failure response. Returns (pay_msg, pay_code) tuple or (None, None) for draft.

`put_basic_checks(identifier, filing_id, client_request, business)` validates PUT/POST preconditions. Requires JSON body (400 if absent); forbids POST with filing_id (403); requires filing/header/name (400 if absent); requires valid business unless filing_type in NEW_BUSINESS_FILING_TYPES (400 if missing). No caller check shown.

`check_authorization(identifier, filing_json, business, filing_id)` enforces access control. Extracts filing_type and sub_type; uses business state (or ACTIVE if None) and legal_type from business or nameRequest. Calls `authorized(identifier, jwt, action=['edit'])` and `is_allowed(business, state, filing_type, legal_type, jwt, filing_sub_type, filing_id)`, returns 401 if either fails. No caller check shown.

structured.condensed: Supports filing operations for a business registration system, checking filing history and managing COLIN-sourced filings. Entry points: `is_before_epoch_filing(filing_json, business)` — no check shown — returns true if filing date precedes the business's epoch filing. `is_historical_colin_filing(filing_json)` — no check shown — returns true if filing source is COLIN and date is before BOB_DATE constant. `process_colin_filing(identifier, filing, business)` — no check shown — if filing has colin_event_ids, either links filing to epoch filing's transaction and marks processed and saves, or publishes filing to queue; returns response tuple. `save_filing(request, business_identifier, user, filing_id)` — no check shown — creates or updates Filing; extracts JSON from request, finds business (or bootstrap if identifier starts 'T'), sets submitter_id, sanitizes HTML fields, parses source (COLIN or LEAR default), calls _save_colin_event_ids if COLIN source, sets filing and effective dates, saves to database, returns business/bootstrap, filing, errors dict, HTTP status. `_save_colin_filing` called on COLIN source: parses filing_date and appends ColinEventId objects for each colinId in header, returns error tuple if KeyError. `sanitize_html_fields(filing_json)` — no check shown — sanitizes specialResolution.resolution and correction.resolution fields via Sanitizer to prevent XSS. `validate_filing_json(request)` — no check shown — validates request JSON against 'filing' schema via rsbc_schemas, returns validation message or error array. GOTCHA: no authorization check on save_filing despite user parameter; no duplicate guard on COLIN event IDs; exception handling in process_colin_filing catches all exceptions broadly and returns generic error.

Entry point: `get_filing_types` (static method, called by unknown callers—this chunk shows no check). Reads from input `filing_json` dict to extract header flags (priority, waiveFees), filing type name, and nested filing details; reads `business.legal_type`. Routes on filing type: if correction-type key present, looks up filing code by legal type and returns one entry; if dissolution, branches on dissolutionType (voluntary adds futureEffective and for COOP legal type adds special resolution and affidavit codes; administrative returns NOFEE); if courtOrder/registrarsNotation/registrarsOrder/putBackOn/adminFreeze, returns code and description; else iterates all filing keys, looking up sub-type, checking if changeOfDirectors is free (only nameChanged or addressChanged actions), and whether priority applies (disabled for changeOfDirectors/changeOfAddress under annualReport). Appends futureEffective only for incorporationApplication/amalgamationApplication/continuationIn/alteration. Returns list of dicts, each with filingTypeCode, priority, waiveFees, and conditionally futureEffective or filingDescription. GOTCHA: no permission check; changeOfDirectors free determination scans all directors but breaks at first non-free one—inconsistent whether to check all or any.

structured.condensed:
Creates an invoice via payment service and records the payment token on a business filing. Entry point: `create_invoice` (static method, called by request handlers); no permission check shown. Gets filing type, extracts or derives mailing address and corporate type from filing JSON (new business, conversion, or standard rules); special handling for new business and conversion types. Builds payload with business info (identifier, legal name, mailing address fields), filing info (id, types, optional folioNumber), and invoice details (registration or incorporation number). If caller has STAFF_ROLE or SYSTEM_ROLE (checked via `user_jwt.validate_roles`), adds optional accountInfo fields from filing header: routingSlipNumber, bcolAccountNumber, datNumber. POSTs payload to PAYMENT_SVC_URL with Bearer token and 20-second timeout; catches ConnectionError and Timeout, logs, returns error 402. On 200/201: extracts payment id and statusCode from response JSON, saves payment_token, payment_status_code, payment_account (from param), submitter_roles on filing, returns isPaymentActionRequired flag and 201. On 400: extracts error type and detail from response, saves payment_status_code, returns both and 402. Otherwise returns error and 402.

`set_effective_date`: sets effectiveDate on filing to tomorrow 1 minute after midnight for changeOfAddress (non-COOP only); calls `LegislationDatetime.tomorrow_one_minute_after_midnight()`, converts to UTC, updates filing JSON, saves.

`is_future_effective_filing`: returns True if filing.effectiveDate (parsed ISO) > current UTC time.

`delete_from_minio`: conditionally deletes files from MinioService by fileKey from filing JSON based on filing type: incorporationApplication/alteration (rulesFileKey, memorandumFileKey), dissolution (affidavitFileKey), courtOrder (fileKey), continuationIn (affidavitFileKey under foreignJurisdiction, all fileKeys in authorization.files array).

`details_for_invoice`: returns empty list if business_identifier is null or starts with 'T'; otherwise returns label-value pair: "Registration Number:" for SP/GP, else "Incorporation Number:", with business_identifier as value.

GOTCHA: `create_invoice` saves filing state after payment token is received, but does not retry if save fails; connection errors are logged but not retried.

structured.condensed:
Retrieves pending tasks and to-do items for a business filing, including draft/incomplete filings, annual reports due, and name request incorporation tasks.

Entry point: `GET /<identifier>/tasks` requires JWT auth; checks identifier is valid (if it starts with 'NR', validates via Namex that the name request is consumable, returns 403 if not). Flow: if identifier is NR and no business exists, creates incorporate-NR to-do; if business exists, constructs task list from draft/incomplete/pending/error filings (order 1+), checks for missing required business info and if so adds conversion-filing to-do, and for non-SP/GP businesses appends annual report to-dos for each year from next_ar_year up to current year where ar_min_date has passed (enabled only if no pending filings and ar_min_date is in start_year). For each pending filing with payment_status_code='CREATED' and payment_token, calls payment service to fetch isPaymentActionRequired and paymentMethod and adds to filing header. Returns jsonify(tasks=rv) or error: if is_consumable is false returns 403 with validation details; if payment service fails (ConnectionError or Timeout) returns SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE with message. Task objects contain task (filing json or todo structure), order, enabled.

Helpers: `construct_task_list()` builds task list, `create_todo()` shapes annual report to-do, `create_incorporate_nr_todo()` shapes name request to-do, `create_conversion_filing_todo()` shapes conversion to-do.

structured.condensed: Returns completed filings to Colin sync service, formatted as JSON with business details and metadata. Entry point `GET /internal/filings` requires `UserRoles.colin` role (checked by `@jwt.has_one_of_roles`); caller is internal job `update_colin_filings`. Paginates by `page` and `limit` query params. Fetches filings via `Filing.get_completed_filings_for_colin()`, excludes type `lear_epoch` and coop corrections. Adds `filingId`, `filing.header.date` (as ISO string), `filing.header.learEffectiveDate` (as ISO string). Populates missing `filing.business` from `VersionedBusinessDetailsService.get_business_revision_obj(filing.transaction_id, business.id)` if transaction_id exists, else from `business.json()`; adds `legalName` if absent. For `amalgamationApplication` with type `horizontal` or `vertical`: calls `set_from_primary_or_holding_business_data()` (catches and logs exceptions, skips filing on error—swallowed). Flask routes that track and update Colin legal database event IDs, and manage tax IDs for businesses. Requires UserRoles.colin authentication on all endpoints.

GET /internal/filings/colin_id returns the last updated Colin event ID from colin_last_update table, or a specific entry if colin_id parameter provided. POST /internal/filings/colin_id/<int:colin_id> inserts a new row into colin_last_update with current timestamp and the provided event ID, then returns the last updated ID. Decision: if colin_id parameter supplied, queries ColinEventId by colin_id and returns colin_event_id field; otherwise queries colin_last_update table ordered by id descending and returns last_event_id. Returns 404 if no records found.

GET /internal/tax_ids calls Business.get_all_by_no_tax_id(), iterates results, returns list of identifier fields. POST /internal/tax_ids reads JSON body as dict of identifier:tax_id pairs, finds each Business by identifier, sets tax_id field and saves. Logs error if Business not found but continues processing other identifiers.

GOTCHA: POST /internal/filings/colin_id uses raw f-string SQL injection vulnerability with colin_id parameter. GOTCHA: POST /internal/filings/colin_id has malformed return tuple on error (missing colon in dict key). GOTCHA: GET /internal/filings/colin_id catches broad Exception and re-raises without saving transaction state. GOTCHA: POST /internal/tax_ids has no duplicate guard and processes silently if identifier not found in database.

structured.condensed:
API endpoint handler for retrieving and creating comments on business filings. Provides GET and POST operations scoped to a business identifier and filing ID.

GET returns all comments for a filing, or a single comment by ID if provided. POST creates a new comment attached to a filing. Both check that the business and filing exist via `_basic_checks()`. POST additionally checks `authorized(identifier, jwt, action=['add_comment'])` and enforces that the filing ID in the JSON request body matches the URL parameter. It validates the comment payload via `validate(json_input, True)`, rejects if payload's `filingId` differs from URL `filing_id`, retrieves or creates the current user from JWT token info, then saves the comment with `comment.save()`. GET with identifier starting with 'T' loads business via `Filing.get_temp_reg_filing()` and `Business.find_by_internal_id()`, otherwise via `Business.find_by_identifier()`. The PUT, PATCH, DELETE route for versioned API calls is blocked with METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED. POST returns HTTPStatus.CREATED on success; exceptions raised by `comment.save()` return the error status code or default to CREATED/ACCEPTED. No retry, no deduplication check shown.

GOTCHA: authorization check condition `action=['add_comment']` is not shown to enforce who may perform it. GOTCHA: exception handling in POST catches `BusinessException` but swallows it; only logs via reply object. GOTCHA: `_basic_checks()` finds business differently for identifier starting 'T' but logs no explanation of this special case.

structured.condensed:
Flask Blueprint providing three document endpoints for draft filings stored in Minio object storage. Incoming requests carry JWT authorization via requires_auth decorator, required for all routes.

GET /<file_name>/signatures calls MinioService.create_signed_put_url(file_name) and returns a pre-signed URL with status 200, enabling clients to upload a new document.

DELETE /<document_key> deletes a document only if its filing status equals Filing.Status.DRAFT.value. The check is: calls is_draft_filing(document_key), which queries Document by file_key, then Filing by document.filing_id, returns True if no document exists or filing status is DRAFT. If the check passes, calls MinioService.delete_file(document_key) and returns success message with 200; if filing is not draft, returns 403 FORBIDDEN; on any exception, logs error and returns 500. No transaction guard; deletion proceeds without re-querying the filing state immediately before the delete call.

GET /<document_key> retrieves a document by calling MinioService.get_file(document_key), returns response.data as application/pdf with response.status; on exception, logs error and returns 500. No check whether the document belongs to a draft filing.

GOTCHA: DELETE enforces draft-only deletion via is_draft_filing check; GET has no such guard and will retrieve documents from non-draft filings. GOTCHA: DELETE is not transactional—filing status could change between is_draft_filing check and MinioService.delete_file call.

uses.what: Called with document_key to retrieve the document from Minio and return its data and status.

Internal service API routes for scheduled filing operations and tax ID updates in a business registry system.

Entry points: `GET /api/v2/internal/filings/future_effective` requires `system` role (checked via `@jwt.has_one_of_roles([UserRoles.system])`); returns filing IDs from `Filing.get_future_effective_filing_ids()` as JSON array with HTTP 200. `POST /api/v2/internal/bnmove` requires `system` role; reads `oldBn` and `newBn` from JSON body, returns HTTP 400 if either missing. Main flow: looks up business by `old_bn` via `Business.find_by_tax_id(old_bn)`, updates its `tax_id` field to `new_bn`, saves it. Calls `create_registrars_notation_filing(business, user, old_bn)` which builds a Filing object with `filing_json` containing header (name: 'registrarsNotation', certifiedBy: 'system'), business identifier and legal type, registrars notation order details describing the BN change "based on a request from the CRA"; saves filing; calls `ListFilingResource.complete_filing()` and returns response code—if not HTTP 201, logs error but continues. Publishes two events: `bc.registry.bnmove` with oldBn/newBn to NATS_EMAILER_SUBJECT config, and `bc.registry.business.bn` with empty payload to NATS_ENTITY_EVENT_SUBJECT config. Returns HTTP 200 success message regardless of business lookup result; if business not found, only logs error. GOTCHA: no check that `create_registrars_notation_filing()` succeeds before returning OK; if business not found, endpoint still returns 200 with success message.

Entry points: static methods callable by any component (this chunk shows no permission check). No error handling shown; stream operations not wrapped in try-finally; no duplicate guard on key generation.

structured.condensed:
Flask extension that publishes JSON payloads to a NATS/STAN message queue.

Entry point: `publish_json(payload, subject)` called from anywhere in the Flask app, with no check shown; also `publish_json_to_subject(payload, subject)` for async callers. Both methods accept optional subject (defaults to `NATS_FILER_SUBJECT` config value) and optional payload dict.

Flow: On first call, `connect()` establishes NATS client with options from config (`NATS_SERVERS`, `NATS_CLUSTER_ID`, `NATS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `NATS_CLIENT_NAME`) and a derived `client_id` (lowercased name with punctuation replaced by underscores, plus random bits). Payload is JSON-encoded and UTF-8 encoded, then published via `stan.publish()` to the subject. Errors are logged and re-raised; no retry shown.

On Flask teardown, `close()` closes STAN then NATS if connected. Clients are cached in Flask's `g` object (request scope) or instance variables `_nats`, `_stan`. Connection state checked via `nats.is_connected`. Callbacks (`on_error`, `on_disconnect`, `on_reconnect`, `on_close`) log warnings when triggered by the client library.

GOTCHA: no permission check; callers can publish to any subject. GOTCHA: errors are re-raised after logging, no transactional guarantee that message reached the queue before an exception occurs.

Health-check probe service that exposes three HTTP endpoints to report NATS and STAN service liveliness to Kubernetes or similar orchestrators.

Initialized with an event loop, logger, host (default '0.0.0.0'), port (default 7070), and an optional list of components. Starts an aiohttp web server on GET /healthz, /readyz, /meta. 

/healthz returns {status: 'healthy'} with status 200 if all components report `await component.is_healthy` true; else {status: 'unhealthy'} with 503. If no components provided, always returns 503.

/readyz returns {status: 'ready'} with status 200 if all components report `await component.is_ready` true; else {status: 'not ready'} with 503. If no components provided, always returns 503.

/meta returns JSON with 'probe' set to __version__ from entity_queue_common.version, plus each component's class name mapped to its __version__, and if the component has a name attribute, that name mapped to its version attribute.

start() logs 'Starting web probe v{__version__}', creates AppRunner, binds to host:port, logs "Liveliness probe listening at '{host} : {port}'", and returns a set {host, port}. stop() stops the site if running. This chunk shows no permission or authentication check on any endpoint.

uses.name: component.name
uses.what: Optional component attribute; if present, mapped to component.version in metadata response.

structured.condensed: Manages listening to and handling messages from a NATS/STAN queue stream. ServiceWorker wraps a service that connects to NATS and STAN, subscribes to a queue via config-supplied options (NATS_CONNECTION_OPTIONS, STAN_CONNECTION_OPTIONS, SUBSCRIPTION_OPTIONS), and invokes a callback handler (cb_handler) when messages arrive. On connection loss, retries reconnection up to 100 times with full client reinstatiation; all errors during reconnect are caught and logged, loop continues. Offers is_healthy and is_ready properties (both check nc.is_connected). QueueServiceManager orchestrates: starts Probes component health checks, connects ServiceWorker, registers SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers calling signal_handler. Errors during startup are caught and logged only; no halt on failure. GOTCHA: reconnect loop catches all exceptions and continues silently without backoff, risking busy-loop. GOTCHA: startup errors do not prevent event loop from running. GOTCHA: no check shown on whether callback handler is callable.

structured.condensed:
Email publisher for entity filing notifications. Subscribes to filing events via NATS, transforms them into email payloads using filing-type-specific processors, and publishes to the notification service.

Entry point is `cb_subscription_handler` (entry point not shown in chunk). The handler receives messages from the queue, looks up the Filing and Furnishing records by ID, dispatches to the appropriate email processor based on filing type, and sends the resulting email payload via `send_email`. The email processors map filings to email recipient lists, subject lines, and body content.

`send_email` validates that the email dict has non-empty `recipients`, `content`, and `content.body`; if not, raises `QueueException`. It POSTs the email to `NOTIFY_API_URL` with an Authorization bearer token; if the response status is not 200, raises `EmailException`. Exceptions are caught and re-raised without further handling—no retry loop is shown.

`publish_event` publishes a payload dict to the NATS subject in `ENTITY_EVENT_PUBLISH_OPTIONS['subject']`; exceptions are logged but not re-raised.

Processors support: affiliation, agm_extension, agm_location_change, amalgamation, ar_reminder, bn, change_of_registration, consent_continuation_out, continuation_in, continuation_out, correction, dissolution, filing, involuntary_dissolution_stage_1, mras, name_request, nr, registration, restoration, special_resolution notifications.

GOTCHA: send_email logs but re-raises EmailException; caller must handle retries. GOTCHA: Exceptions in publish_event are swallowed entirely.

structured.condensed: Queue consumer that processes business registry notification emails. Receives email messages from a NATS queue, routes them by type and option to notification processors, and sends the resulting emails. Entry point is `cb_subscription_handler`, a NATS callback invoked when messages arrive on the queue; this chunk shows no permission check. Calls `AccountService.get_bearer_token()` to get credentials. Extracts `email_msg['type']` and `email_msg['data']['request']['option']` (or `email_msg['email']['type']` and `email_msg['email']['option']` in else branch) to determine flow. For name-request emails with option in BEFORE_EXPIRY, EXPIRED, RENEWAL, UPGRADE, REFUND calls `nr_notification.process()`, otherwise `name_request.process()`. For affiliation type calls `affiliation_notification.process()`. For bnmove calls `bn_notification.process_bn_move()`. For dissolution with furnishingName in PROCESSABLE_FURNISHING_NAMES calls `involuntary_dissolution_stage_1_notification.process()`, sends email, calls `post_process()` with PROCESSED status; on exception calls `post_process()` with FAILED status and re-raises. Routes businessNumber, amalgamationApplication/continuationIn/incorporationApplication with mras option, annualReport with reminder option (reads `disable-specific-service-provider` flag), agmLocationChange/agmExtension with COMPLETED option, dissolution, registration, restoration, changeOfRegistration, correction, consentContinuationOut, continuationOut, specialResolution, and filing types via dedicated processors. Calls `send_email(email, token)` for each. Tracker utility checks if message was previously processed before calling `process_email()`, starts tracking, completes or fails tracking on exceptions. OperationalError and EmailException are re-raised to return message to queue; all other exceptions are caught and logged without re-raise. GOTCHA: broad exception catch (line with `except (QueueException, Exception)`) swallows exceptions without re-raising, so some failures are not retried; OperationalError and EmailException explicitly re-raise. GOTCHA: `post_process()` is called after `send_email()` succeeds, but if `send_email()` fails (raises), `post_process()` with FAILED is called in except block—this means a send failure can trigger the failed-status update.

structured.condensed: Configuration file that loads and provides environment-based settings for a legal filing service. Loads all envars from .env file or environment, then bundles them into configuration classes for development, testing, and production. The module exposes get_named_config(config_name) to return the appropriate config object based on name ('development', 'testing', 'production', or 'staging'); raises KeyError if config_name is unknown. Base _Config class reads venv or defaults for: PostgreSQL connection (DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_NAME, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI); NATS/STAN message queue (NATS_SERVERS, NATS_CLIENT_NAME, NATS_CLUSTER_ID, NATS_FILER_SUBJECT, NATS_QUEUE); topics for entity events (NATS_ENTITY_EVENT_SUBJECT) and email (NATS_EMAILER_SUBJECT); external service URLs (PAYMENT_SVC_URL, COLIN_API, AUTH_SVC_URL, ACCOUNT_SVC_AUTH_URL, LEGAL_API_URL, NAMEX_API, NAICS_API_URL); account service credentials (ACCOUNT_SVC_CLIENT_ID, ACCOUNT_SVC_CLIENT_SECRET, ACCOUNT_SVC_TIMEOUT); GCP Pub/Sub topics (BUSINESS_EVENTS_TOPIC, BUSINESS_PAY_TOPIC, NAMEX_PAY_TOPIC) and credentials (GCP_AUTH_KEY, AUDIENCE, PUBLISHER_AUDIENCE); Minio object storage (MINIO_ENDPOINT, MINIO_ACCESS_KEY, MINIO_ACCESS_SECRET, MINIO_BUCKET_BUSINESSES, MINIO_SECURE); report and fonts paths; Sentry DSN (nullified if string 'null'); LaunchDarkly SDK key; SQLAlchemy settings. STAN client_id uses random.SystemRandom().getrandbits(0x58). TestConfig overrides database vars to use _TEST_ prefixed envars and hardcodes Minio to localhost:9000 with credentials minio/minio123, MINIO_SECURE=False. DevConfig sets TESTING=False, DEBUG=True; ProdConfig sets both False.

structured.condensed:
Processes an incoming amalgamation application filing to create a new amalgamated business entity and records the source businesses being dissolved.

Entry point: `process(business, filing, filing_rec, filing_meta)` receives from the filing queue; this chunk shows no check that the caller may invoke it. Flow: Extracts `filing.filing.amalgamationApplication`; raises `QueueException` if missing or if business already exists. Reserves next corp number via `business_info.get_next_corp_num()`. Creates `Amalgamation` record with `filing_id`, `amalgamation_type` (from filing), `amalgamation_date` (from `filing_rec.effective_date`), and `court_approval` (boolean). Calls `create_amalgamating_businesses()` which iterates `amalgamatingBusinesses`; for each, extracts `role` and `identifier`; if `foreignJurisdiction` present, stores as `foreign_identifier`, `foreign_name`, `foreign_jurisdiction` (country uppercased), `foreign_jurisdiction_region` (if region, uppercased); else looks up local business by identifier and calls `dissolve_amalgamating_business()`. For horizontal or vertical amalgamations, locates holding or primary amalgamating business, copies its legal name, directors (via `_set_parties()` which fetches active directors, rebuilds roles with appointment date), offices (via `_set_offices()` copying registered and records offices), and share structure (via `_set_shares()` copying share classes and resolution dates). Creates new `Business` with state ACTIVE via `business_info.update_business_info()`. Updates filing with offices, parties, shares, aliases, court order. Stores `nrNumber` and `legalName` in `filing_meta.amalgamation_application`. Saves identifier, legal type, founding date to filing JSON. Returns business, filing_rec, filing_meta.

GOTCHA: `create_amalgamating_businesses()` dissolves source businesses on first call only—if a step later fails, dissolution is already recorded but business record creation may not complete.

Processes a change-of-address filing in the entity filing system. Applies office and address updates from the filing to the business model, records the change date, and postpones any in-progress batch dissolutions by 62 days while flagging the delay.

Entry point: `process(business, filing, filing_meta, flag_on)` — callable by filing processors with no visible check. Reads the changeOfAddress.offices object from the filing dict, keyed by office_type. For each office and address type in the filing, the function updates the matching address on the business (via `update_address`) or creates and appends a new one (via `create_address`). Sets business.last_coa_date to filing_meta.application_date.

When flag_on is true, checks if business.in_dissolution. If so, retrieves all BatchProcessing records by business_id and iterates: for each with status other than COMPLETED or WITHDRAWN, and trigger_date within 60 days ahead, sets trigger_date to 62 days from now, adds changeOfAddressDelay: True to meta_data dict, and updates last_modified to utcnow.

Processes change-of-directors filings by applying director appointment, modification, and cessation actions to a business model. Entry point is `process(business, filing, filing_meta)`, callable by any filer workflow with no check shown.

Reads `filing['changeOfDirectors']['directors']` array; for each director, checks if it came from colin via `filing.get('colinIds')`. If so, matches the new director against existing `PartyRole` directors by name (case-insensitive) to determine action: if name matches an active director with no cessation date, action is 'modified'; if name matches a ceased director but new record has no cessation date, action is 'appointed'; if no match, action is 'appointed'; if matched director is cease-dated and new record has cessation date, action is 'ceased'. For action 'appointed', calls `create_party(business_id, party_info)` and `create_role(party, role_info)` to insert new director party role into `business.party_roles`. For actions 'modified', 'ceased', or other non-appointment actions, resolves the director name (using `prevFirstName`, `prevMiddleInitial`, `prevLastName` if action is 'nameChanged'), matches against active directors, and calls `update_director(director, new_info)`. After processing all new directors from colin, ceases any existing active director not in the new list by setting `cessation_date` to `datetime.utcnow()`. Sets `business.last_cod_date` to `filing_meta.application_date`.

Raises `QueueException` if director name cannot be resolved from filing. This chunk shows no permission check. GOTCHA: name comparison concatenates fields without checking for None; middle_initial defaulting to empty string masks that. GOTCHA: for colin filings, active directors absent from new list are auto-ceased without an explicit 'ceased' action in the filing.

Processes a change of registration filing onto business model objects (legal name, nature of business, office address, parties, court orders).

Entry point: `process(business, change_filing_rec, change_filing, filing_meta)` called by external filing processor with no permission check shown. Updates legal name from `changeOfRegistration/nameRequest/legalName` by calling `business_info.set_legal_name`; records old and new names in `filing_meta.change_of_registration`. Updates NAICS code from `changeOfRegistration/business/naics/naicsCode` by calling `business_info.update_naics_info`; records old code, new code, and description. Updates business office address from `changeOfRegistration/offices/businessOffice` values by finding Address by id and calling `update_address`. Updates parties by calling `update_parties(business, party_json, change_filing_rec)`. Updates court order by calling `filings.update_filing_court_order`.

`update_parties` ceases party roles not in incoming list (sets `cessation_date` to current UTC time), then creates or updates each party: if party has no id or a non-integer id, calls `_create_party_info`; else calls `_update_party`.

`_update_party(party_info)` finds Party by integer id, updates first_name, last_name, middle_initial, title, organization_name, party_type, email, identifier (all uppercased except email lowercased), updates or creates delivery_address and mailing_address by calling `create_address` or `update_address`.

`_create_party_info` calls `create_party`, then for each role in `roles` list creates role dict with roleType, appointmentDate, cessationDate; calls `create_role`; if role is COMPLETING_PARTY adds to `change_filing_rec.filing_party_roles`, else adds to `business.party_roles`.

All exceptions suppressed with `contextlib.suppress` in main flow. GOTCHA: no database save shown in `process` or `update_parties` functions, state not persisted after updates. GOTCHA: party update modifies existing Party object without new record creation; delete/cessation handled only via role cessation_date.

Processes a consent continuation out filing by extracting court order, foreign jurisdiction details, and expiry date from the filing JSON, then populates a ConsentContinuationOut database record linked to the business and updates filing metadata.

Caller: Entry point `process(business, cco_filing, filing, filing_meta)` called by entity_filer framework to render consent continuation out filing into business model; this chunk shows no check. Extracts from filing JSON: `/consentContinuationOut/courtOrder` passed to `update_filing_court_order()`, with IndexError/KeyError/TypeError silently suppressed. Reads `foreignJurisdiction.country` (uppercased) and `foreignJurisdiction.region` (uppercased if present, else None). Calls `get_expiry_date(cco_filing)` to compute expiry 6 months after filing effective_date, handling daylight saving time offset drift by converting effective_date and computed date to legislation timezone, calculating DST difference, and applying correction before converting to UTC. Creates ConsentContinuationOut with foreign_jurisdiction, foreign_jurisdiction_region, expiry_date, filing_id, business_id; appends to business.consent_continuation_outs. Sets filing_meta.consent_continuation_out to dict holding 'country', 'region' (both strings), 'expiry' (ISO format string).

GOTCHA: Court order update exception is silently suppressed with `suppress(IndexError, KeyError, TypeError)` — failures are not logged or recorded.
