structured.condensed: Factory to create payment system service instances by payment method or user context. Entry point `create_from_payment_method` takes a payment method string and returns the corresponding service instance (DirectPayService, PaybcService, BcolService, InternalPayService, OnlineBankingService, PadService, EftService, or EjvPayService); this chunk shows no check on caller or payment_method format. Entry point `create` is decorated with `@user_context` and requires `user`, `payment_account`, and `payment_method` in kwargs; caller must pass bcolAccountNumber in account_info if applicable. Main flow: if total_fees is 0, return InternalPayService; else if user has STAFF role and bcolAccountNumber exists, return BcolService; else if user has SYSTEM role and bcolAccountNumber exists, return BcolService; else call create_from_payment_method with payment_method. After instance creation, calls `_validate_and_throw_error` which checks if instance is PadService and if so, compares pad_activation_date against current UTC time and cfs_account_status against PENDING_PAD_ACTIVATION, raising ACCOUNT_IN_PAD_CONFIRMATION_PERIOD if either condition holds. Creates service instances with no per-instance configuration step shown. GOTCHA: date comparison uses pad_activation_date.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) then compares with datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc), risking misalignment if pad_activation_date is already aware. GOTCHA: create_from_payment_method raises INVALID_CORP_OR_FILING_TYPE for unknown payment_method rather than a more specific error.

Audit base class for ORM models to track creation and modification metadata in the pay-api database system.

This abstract SQLAlchemy base class automatically adds four audit columns to any model that inherits from it: `created_on` (timestamps at UTC on insert), `updated_on` (timestamps at UTC on each update), `created_by` (populated by calling `_get_user_name` at insert, stores up to 50 chars), and `updated_by` (populated at update, nullable, up to 50 chars). structured.condensed:
Database model class that records settlement file information received from CAS (usually in CSV format) for payment reconciliation. 

Stores: file name (string, required), received timestamp (datetime, defaults to current UTC time), and optional processed timestamp (datetime). All records have an auto-incrementing integer primary key.

The model uses SQLAlchemy's `include_properties` mapper to explicitly define four fields (id, file_name, processed_on, received_on) in alphabetical order. This strategy enables rolling upgrades by allowing new and old service versions to coexist without breaking if additional fields appear in the database from failed deploys or mid-upgrade states; it avoids the ambiguity of telling SQLAlchemy to silently ignore structural differences, which could interfere with Alembic migrations.

No entry points, decision logic, or external calls; this is a data model only.

Encryption uses current_app.config.get('ACCOUNT_SECRET_KEY'). CfsAccountSchema serializes the model.

Extends Flask-SQLAlchemy's Query class with helper methods for filtering database queries.

Entry points: Three public methods called by query builders. `filter_boolean(search_criteria, model_attribute)` adds a filter for boolean fields—passes through if criteria is False, raises ValueError if None, otherwise filters equality; no caller check shown. `filter_conditionally(search_criteria, model_attribute, is_like)` adds a filter if criteria is not None—converts datetime/date to DATE function comparison, applies case-insensitive ILIKE with wildcard wrapping if is_like=True (using func.lower and func.ilike to prevent SQL injection), otherwise equality; no caller check shown. `filter_conditional_date_range(start_date, end_date, model_attribute)` filters by date range using func.DATE—if both dates present, filters >= start and <= end; if only start, >= start; if only end, <= end; returns query; no caller check shown.

GOTCHA: filter_boolean raises ValueError for None but silently passes through (returns self unchanged) for False, creating asymmetric handling of falsy values.

Stores and queries invoice records in a business filing system with payment and disbursement tracking.

Inherits from Audit. Table `invoices` uses mapper to include 24 named fields, ignoring others during rolling upgrades. Relationships join `payment_line_items`, `receipts`, `payment_account`, `references`, and `corp_type`.

Entry points: five classmethod queries callable by any code—no permission checks shown. `find_invoices_by_status_for_account` filters payment_account_id and invoice_status_code in the list provided, ordered by id. `find_invoices_for_payment` joins InvoiceReference and Payment tables on invoice_number to find invoices where reference_status equals the parameter (default InvoiceReferenceStatus.ACTIVE.value) and Payment.id matches. `find_outstanding_invoices_for_account` filters on payment_account_id and returns invoices with status APPROVED or PARTIAL, or payment_method_code PAD with status PAID created after from_date, or payment_method_code EFT with status APPROVED or OVERDUE created after from_date. `find_by_business_identifier` and `find_invoices_marked_for_delete` filter by one column. `find_created_direct_pay_invoices` filters status CREATED, payment_method_code DIRECT_PAY, and created_on >= (now minus days/hours/minutes).

`update_invoices_for_revenue_updates` takes fee_distribution_id, joins PaymentLineItem, transitions matching invoices: if status PAID → UPDATE_REVENUE_ACCOUNT, if REFUNDED → UPDATE_REVENUE_ACCOUNT_REFUND. Calls `db.session.bulk_save_objects` and `cls.commit()` to persist.

Database schema includes mapper configuration explicitly including id, created_on, invoice_id, invoice_number, is_consolidated, reference_number, status_code to support rolling upgrades when fields may differ between service versions.

SQLAlchemy model storing payment records in the `payments` table. The mapper uses `include_properties` to enable rolling upgrades alongside other service versions.

Columns: id (primary key), payment_system_code, payment_method_code, payment_status_code (all foreign keys); payment_account_id (indexed foreign key); invoice_number, receipt_number, cheque_receipt_number, cons_inv_number (all indexed); is_routing_slip (boolean, defaults False); paid_amount, invoice_amount, paid_usd_amount (numeric); payment_date (DateTime); created_by (defaults 'SYSTEM'). Relationships: payment_system (innerjoin to PaymentSystem), payment_status (innerjoin to PaymentStatusCode).

Query methods (all classmethod, no permission checks shown):
- `find_payment_method_by_payment_id(identifier)`: joins PaymentMethod on Payment.payment_method_code, filters Payment.id == identifier, returns one or none.
- `find_payment_by_invoice_number_and_status(inv_number, payment_status)`: filters on invoice_number and payment_status_code, returns all.
- `find_payment_by_receipt_number(receipt_number)`: filters on receipt_number, returns one or none.
- `find_payment_for_invoice(invoice_id)`: joins InvoiceReference and Invoice, filters on InvoiceReferenceStatus.ACTIVE or COMPLETED, returns one or none.
- `find_payments_for_routing_slip(routing_slip)`: filters receipt_number == routing_slip and is_routing_slip is True, returns all.
- `search_account_payments(auth_account_id, payment_status, page, limit)`: joins PaymentAccount on auth_account_id, outer-joins Invoice via InvoiceReference on invoice_number, optionally filters payment_status_code; if status is FAILED, excludes consolidations by subquery filtering cons_inv_number where status is CREATED and method is CC. Paginates by page/limit, returns items and total count.
- `find_payments_to_consolidate(auth_account_id)`: builds subquery of cons_inv_number where status is FAILED and method is PAD, then joins PaymentAccount on auth_account_id and outer-joins InvoiceReference filtered to ACTIVE status, returns all Payment records where status is FAILED or invoice_number in subquery.

Filters and paginates invoice queries by date, line item descriptions, and JSON detail fields for a search interface.

Receives a query object, auth account ID, search filter dict, limit, and page number. Returns paginated subquery of Invoice IDs grouped and ordered descending.

Date filtering: reads `dateFilter/startDate` and `dateFilter/endDate` (DT_SHORT_FORMAT strings), or `weekFilter/index` (integer), or `monthFilter/month` and `monthFilter/year` (integers). Parses dates and applies timezone conversion (LEGISLATIVE_TIMEZONE from config), truncates start time to 00:00:00 and end time to 23:59:59.999999, filters Invoice.created_on between these bounds.

Details filtering: reads `lineItems`, `details`, or `lineItemsAndDetails` from search_filter. For `lineItems`, outer-joins PaymentLineItem and filters by description case-insensitive substring match. For `details`, joins jsonb_array_elements(Invoice.details) and filters value or label fields case-insensitive match. For `lineItemsAndDetails`, combines both. When is_count is true, uses outerjoin instead of join.

Subquery generation: calls filter() with add_outer_joins=True, groups by Invoice.id, orders descending, applies limit and page offset: (page - 1) * limit.

Model defining Payment Transaction records in a payment processing system. 

Stores transaction state with id (UUID), status_code (CREATED/COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED), payment_id (foreign key), and timestamps (transaction_start_time in UTC, transaction_end_time optional). Also holds client_system_url, pay_system_url, pay_response_url, and pay_system_reason_code (all nullable strings).

Entry points: all are class methods with no permission checks shown.
- find_by_payment_id(payment_id): returns all transactions for a payment.
- find_active_by_payment_id(payment_id): returns one active (CREATED status) transaction for a payment.
- find_active_by_invoice_id(invoice_id): joins through Payment and InvoiceReference to find one active transaction where InvoiceReference status is ACTIVE, returning None if none exists.
- find_recent_completed_by_invoice_id(invoice_id): same joins, filters for COMPLETED status only, returns newest by transaction_end_time descending.
- find_by_invoice_id(invoice_id): same joins, no status filter, returns all.
- find_stale_records(days, hours, minutes): returns incomplete (not COMPLETED/CANCELLED/FAILED) transactions older than the specified elapsed time, joining Payment to filter only CC or DIRECT_PAY payment methods.

Schema serializes status_code, payment_id, and timestamps (aliased to start_time/end_time) with timezone LEGISLATIVE_TIMEZONE.

Filters a folio search query by date range, receipt numbers, folio number, and account name. Four classmethod filters that chain onto a query object.

`_add_date_filter` extracts startDate and endDate from `dateFilter`, parses them as DT_SHORT_FORMAT, sets from-date time to 00:00:00 and to-date to 23:59:59.999999 in LEGISLATIVE_TIMEZONE, then filters the target date column (defaults to routing_slip_date, or uses dateFilter/target if provided) between these bounds using UTC timezone conversion.

`_add_receipt_number` builds OR conditions: if receiptNumber present, filters Payment.cheque_receipt_number matching with payment_method_code==CASH; if chequeReceiptNumber present, filters Payment.cheque_receipt_number matching with payment_method_code==CHEQUE. Both require Payment.payment_account_id==PaymentAccount.id.

`_add_folio_filter` filters Invoice.folio_number matching folioNumber and Invoice.routing_slip==RoutingSlip.number.

`_add_entity_filter` filters PaymentAccount.name case-insensitive substring match on accountName, requiring PaymentAccount.id==RoutingSlip.payment_account_id.

All return the modified query. GOTCHA: no validation that search_filter keys exist before access; get_str_by_path null-returns gracefully but .get() returns None on missing keys, risking silent no-op filters.

Model to manage statements data in a payment system; part of a pay-api service.

Entries: `Statement` (SQLAlchemy ORM class) has classmethod `find_all_statements_by_notification_status(statuses)` — called by cron jobs, no permission check shown — queries all statements matching notification_status_code in the given list. Classmethod `find_all_payments_and_invoices_for_statement(statement_id)` queries all Invoices joined to the statement via StatementInvoices. `StatementSchema` (Marshmallow serializer) has method `payment_methods_to_list(target)` that splits comma-separated payment_methods string to list or returns empty list. `StatementDTO` (data transfer object, defined with @define) has classmethod `from_row(row)` converting a Statement row by adding 8-hour offset to from_date and to_date and returning isoformat strings; has classmethod `dao_to_dict(statement_daos)` converting list of Statement DAOs to list of dicts via StatementDTO.from_row and Converter unstructure/remove_nones.

Flow: Cron jobs call find_all_statements_by_notification_status to get statements for notification processing. Queries pull from `statements` table (columns: id, frequency, statement_settings_id, payment_account_id, from_date, to_date, is_interim_statement, overdue_notification_date, created_on, notification_status_code, notification_date, payment_methods). Serialization converts Statement objects via StatementSchema, rendering dates in LEGISLATIVE_TIMEZONE and payment_methods as list. DTOs add +8 hours to dates when converting to isoformat strings.

GOTCHA: `find_all_statements_by_notification_status` shows no access control; cron job caller must enforce permissions. Classmethod `from_row` applies hardcoded +8 hour offset to dates without timezone context stated.

Schema `StatementRecipientsSchema` auto-serializes the model with `load_instance=True`.

GOTCHA: `delete_all_recipients` does not check permissions or emit a recorded deletion event. GOTCHA: `bulk_save_recipients` commits unconditionally; partial failure mid-bulk leaves inconsistent state.

structured.condensed:
Flask REST API resource for payment account creation, retrieval, update, and deletion in a payment processing system.

**Entry points:** `POST /accounts` creates account, requires SYSTEM role or CREATE_SANDBOX_ACCOUNT role if sandbox flag is true. `GET /accounts/{account_number}` retrieves account, requires EDIT_ROLE or VIEW_ROLE checked via check_auth(). `GET /accounts/search/eft` lists EFT-enabled accounts, requires SYSTEM or MANAGE_EFT role. `PUT /accounts/{account_number}` updates account, requires SYSTEM role. `PATCH /accounts/{account_number}/eft` enables EFT, requires SYSTEM role. `DELETE /accounts/{account_number}` deletes account, requires SYSTEM role and EDIT_ROLE or VIEW_ROLE via check_auth(). `GET /accounts/{account_number}/fees` retrieves fees, requires MANAGE_ACCOUNTS role. `POST /accounts/{account_number}/fees` creates/updates fees, requires MANAGE_ACCOUNTS role. `PUT /accounts/{account_number}/fees/{product}` sets product fee, requires MANAGE_ACCOUNTS role. `DELETE /accounts/{account_number}/fees` removes fees, requires MANAGE_ACCOUNTS role.

**Input validation:** POST/PUT account creation validates against 'account_info' schema; POST/PUT/DELETE fees validate against 'account_fees' or 'account_fee' schema. Invalid format returns Error.INVALID_REQUEST with serialized errors.

**Main flow:** Account create calls PaymentAccountService.create(request_json, is_sandbox), returns HTTPStatus.ACCEPTED if cfs_account_status is PENDING else CREATED. Account update calls PaymentAccountService.update(account_number, request_json), returns ACCEPTED if pending else OK. Account delete calls PaymentAccountService.delete_account(account_number). EFT enable calls PaymentAccountService.enable_eft(account_number). Fee operations call PaymentAccountService.get_account_fees(), save_account_fees(), delete_account_fees(), save_account_fee().

**Exceptions:** BusinessException and ServiceUnavailableException caught and converted to responses; note that delete_account and get_account call check_auth() but decorators also specify @_jwt.has_one_of_roles([Role.SYSTEM.value]), creating potential mismatch—decorator requires SYSTEM while check_auth only validates EDIT_ROLE or VIEW_ROLE.

**GOTCHA:** delete_account and get_account have conflicting auth: decorator requires SYSTEM role but code calls check_auth(one_of_roles=[EDIT_ROLE, VIEW_ROLE]), so only SYSTEM users can reach check_auth call.

uses.what: Decorator enforcing role-based access control with list of allowed roles.

structured.condensed: Two Flask routes in a business registry payment API that query and report on purchase history. POST `/<account_number>/payments/queries` searches transactions after validating the request schema; requires EDITOR role, or EDITOR plus VIEW_ALL_TRANSACTIONS role if the querystring `viewAll=true` to search all accounts instead of just the given one; calls `Payment.search_purchase_history()` with the account (None if viewAll), request body, page (default 1), and limit (default 10); returns matching rows and HTTP 200. POST `/<account_number>/payments/reports` generates a PDF or CSV report; validates the same schema; requires EDITOR role; reads Accept header to set content type (default PDF); calls `Payment.create_payment_report()` with account, request body, content type, and a report name built from the current UTC date; returns the report as a file attachment with Content-Disposition and Content-Type headers; catches BusinessException and returns its response. Both require JWT auth. GOTCHA: the role check in queries uses `all_of_roles` parameter (must have both when viewAll), while reports use `contains_role` with a variable EDIT_ROLE that this chunk does not define.

structured.condensed: Flask resource providing three REST endpoints to retrieve account statements. All endpoints require JWT authentication and `EDIT_ROLE` authorization for the account. `GET /accounts/<account_id>/statements` returns paginated statement records (default page 1, limit 10) filtered by owing status if supplied; calls StatementService.find_by_account_id with page, limit, is_owing. `GET /accounts/<account_id>/statements/<statement_id>` generates and returns a statement report in the content type requested via Accept header (defaults to PDF); calls StatementService.get_statement_report with statement_id, content_type, and auth; sets Content-Disposition attachment header with filename. `GET /accounts/<account_id>/statements/summary` returns a statement summary with under-payment calculated; calls StatementService.get_summary with auth_account_id and calculate_under_payment=True. All endpoints check authorization via check_auth requiring EDIT_ROLE; this chunk shows the authorization check but never verifies account ownership or resource existence before retrieving. Responses logged at entry and exit.

GET /accounts/{account_id}/statements/notifications retrieves notification details for the account; POST updates them. GET calls StatementRecipients.find_statement_notification_details. Both check authorization via check_auth with account_id; POST catches BusinessException and returns its response. GOTCHA: no indication whether StatementRecipients updates are transactional, or whether duplicate guard exists on POST.

All endpoints accept CORS and validate Role.MANAGE_GL_CODES.value. No check shown for duplicate creation.

Flask REST resource for querying and modifying EFT short names and their account links.

Entry points all require authentication and Role.SYSTEM or Role.MANAGE_EFT; the chunk shows `@_jwt.requires_auth` and `@_jwt.has_one_of_roles([Role.SYSTEM.value, Role.MANAGE_EFT.value])` decorators enforcing this. One route (`post_eft_shortname_link`, `get_eft_shortname_links`) has `@_jwt.has_one_of_roles` only, missing `@_jwt.requires_auth`.

GET /eft-shortnames searches by short_name_id, account_id, account_id_list, account_name, account_branch, amount_owing, short_name, short_name_type, statement_id, state, page, limit; delegates to EFTShortnameService.search, returns paginated response with HTTP 200.

GET /eft-shortnames/summaries searches by short_name_id, payment_received_start_date, payment_received_end_date, credits_remaining, linked_accounts_count, short_name, short_name_type, page, limit; delegates to EFTShortnameSummariesService.search, returns HTTP 200.

GET /eft-shortnames/{short_name_id} calls EFTShortnameService.find_by_short_name_id, returns HTTP 200 or 404.

PATCH /eft-shortnames/{short_name_id} validates request_json against 'eft_short_name' schema; on failure returns Error.INVALID_REQUEST; on BusinessException returns exception.response(); else calls EFTShortnameService.patch_shortname, returns HTTP 200.

GET /eft-shortnames/{short_name_id}/history queries EFTShortnameHistoryService.search with page (default 1), limit (default 10), returns HTTP 200.

GET /eft-shortnames/{short_name_id}/links checks find_by_short_name_id, calls EFTShortnameService.get_shortname_links, returns HTTP 200 or 404.

POST /eft-shortnames/{short_name_id}/links extracts accountId from JSON, checks find_by_short_name_id, calls EFTShortnameService.create_shortname_link, returns HTTP 200 or 404.

PATCH /eft-shortnames/{short_name_id}/links/{short_name_link_id} calls find_link_by_id, checks link exists and link['short_name_id'] matches short_name_id, calls EFTShortnameService.patch_shortname_link, returns HTTP 200 or 404.

POST /eft-shortnames/{short_name_id}/payment checks find_by_short_name_id, validates request_json against 'eft_payment' schema, calls EFTShortnameService.process_payment_action, returns HTTP 204.

structured.condensed: Three routes that manage EFT short name refunds in a Flask API. GET /shortname-refund retrieves refunds for users holding EFT_REFUND or EFT_REFUND_APPROVER roles, parsing query parameters into EFTShortNameRefundGetRequest and returning results from EFTRefundService.get_shortname_refunds(). POST /shortname-refund creates a refund by validating the JSON payload against the 'refund_shortname' schema; if invalid, returns INVALID_REQUEST error; if valid, calls EFTRefundService.create_shortname_refund() and returns ACCEPTED or a BusinessException response. PATCH /shortname-refund/<eft_refund_id> updates a refund (EFT_REFUND_APPROVER only, after JWT auth), converting JSON to EFTShortNameRefundPatchRequest, checking EFTRefundService.find_refund_by_id() first—if found, calls update_shortname_refund() and returns OK; if not found, returns empty body with NOT_FOUND. All routes allow CORS from '*'. GOTCHA: PATCH checks refund exists but does not guard against race conditions between the check and update. GOTCHA: POST schema validation errors are returned without naming the invalid_params structure.

structured.condensed:
Flask REST API resource for Financial and Administrative Services (FAS) routing slip management. Provides six endpoints with role-based access: create (FAS_CREATE), search (FAS_SEARCH), retrieve daily report (FAS_REPORTS), get by number (FAS_VIEW), update (FAS_EDIT), and link parent–child slips (FAS_LINK). Also handles slip comments with view and create endpoints (FAS_VIEW).

Inbound: JSON payloads for routing_slip schema or routing_slip_search_request schema; search includes optional page (default 1) and limit (default 10) integers; patch endpoint takes action query param and JSON body; comment endpoints accept comment or nested comment_bcrs_schema; date and routing_slip_number as URL path parameters. 

Outbound: JSON responses with HTTPStatus codes (CREATED 201, OK 200, NO_CONTENT 204); report endpoint returns PDF binary with Content-Disposition attachment header and filename {file_name}.pdf.

Flow: (1) POST / creates routing slip via RoutingSlipService.create(request_json); (2) POST /queries searches via RoutingSlipService.search(request_json, page, limit, return_all), return_all=true when page param absent; (3) POST /{date}/reports generates daily report via RoutingSlipService.create_daily_reports(date) returning PDF and filename; (4) GET /{routing_slip_number} retrieves via RoutingSlipService.validate_and_find_by_number(routing_slip_number), returns NO_CONTENT if empty; (5) PATCH /{routing_slip_number} updates via RoutingSlipService.update(routing_slip_number, action, body); (6) GET /{routing_slip_number}/links returns parent/child details via RoutingSlipService.get_links(routing_slip_number); (7) POST /links links child to parent via RoutingSlipService.do_link(childRoutingSlipNumber, parentRoutingSlipNumber); (8) GET /{routing_slip_number}/comments retrieves via CommentService.find_all_comments_for_a_routingslip(routing_slip_number); (9) POST /{routing_slip_number}/comments creates via CommentService.create(comment_value, rs_number).

Decisions: Comment POST accepts two schemas (comment or comment_bcrs_schema); tries first schema, if invalid tries second nested comment field; returns INVALID_REQUEST if both fail. Search returns all results when page param missing (return_all=true). Report returns NO_CONTENT on empty response; GET endpoints return empty dict {} on no data.

Access control: Each endpoint enforces role check via @_jwt.has_one_of_roles([roles...]). Callers checked: POST / requires Role.FAS_CREATE, POST /queries requires Role.FAS_SEARCH, POST /{date}/reports requires Role.FAS_REPORTS, GET /{number} requires Role.FAS_VIEW, PATCH /{number} requires Role.FAS_EDIT, GET /{number}/links requires Role.FAS_VIEW or Role.FAS_LINK, POST /links requires Role.FAS_LINK, GET /{number}/comments requires Role.FAS_VIEW, POST /{number}/comments requires Role.FAS_VIEW.

Request payloads validated against schemas; invalid format returns Error.INVALID_REQUEST with serialized errors. BusinessException and ServiceUnavailableException caught and returned as .response(). No duplicate guard, no retry, no transaction scope shown. GOTCHA: comment POST accepts two different request schemas without documenting which clients send which.

GET retrieves invoices by optional businessIdentifier; POST creates invoice from validated JSON body, checking auth via check_auth with business_identifier and corp_type_code against MAKE_PAYMENT role. GET /{invoice_id} retrieves a single invoice by id. DELETE /{invoice_id} soft-deletes via PaymentService.accept_delete. PATCH /{invoice_id} updates payment method from validated JSON body, optionally applying credit if applyCredit query param is 'true'. POST /{invoice_id}/reports generates and returns PDF invoice with Content-Disposition and Content-Type headers set. Exceptions (BusinessException, ServiceUnavailableException) caught and returned via .response(). Validation errors caught and returned via error_to_response. All routes log entry and exit. GOTCHA: PATCH endpoint comment says "Update the payment method for an online banking" but actually updates payment info and may apply credit; description does not match behaviour.

Both routes require JWT authentication and check authorization: GET requires MAKE_PAYMENT, EDIT_ROLE or VIEW_ROLE; POST requires MAKE_PAYMENT. Staff with STAFF and CREATE_CREDITS roles create credits via EFT or DRAWDOWN payment methods after validating payload against 'payment' schema. Non-staff create account payments via PaymentService.create_account_payment, with optional retry, outstanding balance, and invoice status flags controlled by enable-eft-payment-method feature flag. Both responses return payment or receipt object as JSON with HTTP 200 (GET) or 201 (POST). GOTCHA: POST branches on user roles without persisting state before potential service call failure; no retry or failure recording shown for account payment creation.

structured.condensed: Flask REST resource providing transaction endpoints for a payment system. Accepts GET requests to retrieve all transactions for an invoice via `GET /payment-requests/<invoice_id>/transactions` (requires auth) or a single transaction via `GET /payment-requests/<invoice_id>/transactions/<transaction_id>` (requires auth). POST requests create transactions via `POST /payment-requests/<invoice_id>/transactions` or `POST /payments/<payment_id>/transactions`, validating input against 'transaction_request' schema; returns 400 with `Error.INVALID_REQUEST` if invalid, otherwise calls `TransactionService.create_transaction_for_invoice` or `.create_transaction_for_payment` and returns 201 with transaction dict or catches `BusinessException` and returns its response. PATCH requests update transactions via `PATCH /payment-requests/<invoice_id>/transactions/<transaction_id>` or `PATCH /payments/<payment_id>/transactions/<transaction_id>`, extracting `payResponseUrl` from JSON body, calling `TransactionService.update_transaction` and returning 200 with transaction dict or `BusinessException` response. structured.condensed: Authorization service that checks user permission for business entities and accounts, returning authorization details. Entry point `check_auth` decorated with `@user_context` checks if a user may access a business or account; any caller may invoke it with business_identifier, account_id, corp_type_code, and role/premium requirements. For system users with EDITOR role, checks product_code match; for non-BUSINESS products skips remote auth. For others, sends bearer token to AUTH_API_ENDPOINT (either `/orgs/{account_id}/authorizations` or `/entities/{business_identifier}/authorizations`) with optional Product-Code header, receives roles and account details. Makes authorization decision via `one_of_roles` (any match), `contains_role` (exact match), `all_of_roles` (all present), or `is_premium` (account type in PREMIUM_ACCOUNT_TYPES). Sets g.account_id and g.user_permission. Aborts 403 if unauthorized. Fallback for staff with unaffiliated business: stubs account as `PASSCODE_ACCOUNT_{business_identifier}`. Entry point `get_account_admin_users` sends bearer token to AUTH_API_ENDPOINT `/orgs/{auth_account_id}/members?status=ACTIVE&roles=ADMIN`; this chunk shows no caller check. Entry point `get_emails_with_keycloak_role` calls `get_users_with_keycloak_role`, which sends service account token to AUTH_API_ENDPOINT `/keycloak/users?role={role}`. Checks feature flag `override-eft-refund-emails`; if set returns that value, else joins user emails. `get_service_account_token` uses KEYCLOAK_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID and KEYCLOAK_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SECRET to obtain access_token via POST to JWT_OIDC_ISSUER with Basic auth. GOTCHA: check_auth has no caller enforcement in this chunk. GOTCHA: get_account_admin_users shows no caller check.

structured.condensed:
Sends a refund notification to the mailer queue for an invoice payment, and marks an invoice as paid with its receipt.

`_publish_refund_to_mailer` (static method, no check shown) retrieves the receipt, completed invoice reference, and recent completed payment transaction for the invoice, then constructs a payload with identifier, orderNumber (receipt number), transactionDateTime (receipt date if DRAWDOWN method, else transaction end time), transactionAmount, transactionId (invoice number), refundDate (today), and filingDescription (comma-joined payment line item descriptions). For DRAWDOWN payment method, adds bcolAccount, bcolUser (from payment account), and appends invoice number to filingDescription. Publishes the message to the mailer queue via gcp_queue_publisher with source PAY_API, type REFUND_DRAWDOWN_REQUEST, and topic from ACCOUNT_MAILER_TOPIC config.

`complete_payment` (no check shown) creates a Payment record with method and system codes, status COMPLETED, invoice number, total amount, and payment account; sets invoice status to PAID, paid amount to total, payment_date to now; sets invoice reference status to COMPLETED; creates and saves a Receipt with invoice number, amount, invoice id, and current date.

GOTCHA: `_publish_refund_to_mailer` shows no check that the receipt, invoice reference, or payment transaction exist before use. GOTCHA: `complete_payment` updates invoice and invoice_reference but saves only the Receipt; invoice and invoice_reference updates may be lost if a later step fails.

structured.condensed: Provides two decorators that bypass downstream payment systems (BCOL, CFS) and mark invoices complete when a sandbox user context is detected. `skip_invoice_for_sandbox` intercepts invoice creation; if the user's sandbox flag is true, it logs the bypass and returns a fake `InvoiceReference` with sandbox-prefixed IDs instead of calling the wrapped function. `skip_complete_post_invoice_for_sandbox` intercepts post-invoice completion; if sandbox is true, it logs the bypass, calls `complete_payment` and `_release_payment` on the `PaymentSystemService` instance, and returns None instead of invoking the wrapped function. Both decorators extract the `user` from `func_kwargs`, check `user.is_sandbox()`, and pass through to the wrapped function if the check fails. GOTCHA: both decorators access positional arguments by hardcoded index (3 for invoice in first decorator, 0, 1, 2 in second) with no validation; the comment in the first decorator acknowledges this fragility. GOTCHA: the second decorator calls `_release_payment` on a protected method with an explicit pylint disable, signalling bypass of encapsulation.

uses.what: Called from second decorator when sandbox is true; receives invoice and invoice reference arguments.

uses.what: Called from second decorator when sandbox is true via protected-access call; receives invoice argument.

structured.condensed: Service to create invoices in PayBC (BCOL) and manage refunds. Entry point: `create_invoice()` (called by payment system with `@user_context` decorator; this chunk shows no check on whether caller is authorized for the account). Receives payment account, line items, and invoice; generates invoice number and constructs payload with user ID, amount, folio number, remarks, and fee code determined by service fee amount, corp type, and whether user is staff. Payload includes `forceUseDebitAccount=true` for CSBPDOC filing types or if `force_non_staff_fee_code` is passed. For staff users or service account, uses staff fee code and includes additional fields (accountNumber, formNumber, reduntantFlag, rateType). POSTs to `BCOL_API_ENDPOINT/payments` with bearer token; on success, creates and returns InvoiceReference with response key and sequenceNo. On HTTPError, logs error (as error if BCOL_ERROR or BCOL_UNAVAILABLE, else as warning), then raises BusinessException. `get_receipt()` returns invoice number, current timestamp, and invoice total. `process_cfs_refund()` publishes to mailer, sets payment status to REFUNDED, flushes (no commit shown). `complete_post_invoice()` calls `complete_payment()` and `_release_payment()`. Fee code logic: staff → staff_fee_code; else if service_fees in (1.5, 1.05) → full_service_fee; if 1 → partial_service_fee; if 0 → no_service_fee; else logs error and defaults to full_service_fee. GOTCHA: `flush()` called without explicit commit; error handling logs but raises uniformly as BusinessException; remarks field truncated to 50 chars silently; no duplicate guard on invoice creation.

Service to create and manage CFS (Canadian Financial System) accounts in PayBC. Entry points: `create_cfs_account` (classmethod, no check shown), `get_site`, `update_site_receipt_method`, and `validate_bank_account` (all static, no checks shown).

**create_cfs_account**: receives identifier, contact_info dict, optional payment_info dict, receipt_method string, site_name, is_fas boolean. Calls `get_token()` for access_token, then `_create_party()` with prefixed identifier, `_create_paybc_account()` passing is_fas to select CFS_CUSTOMER_PROFILE_CLASS or CFS_FAS_CUSTOMER_PROFILE_CLASS, `_create_site()` passing contact info and is_fas. Returns dict with party_number, account_number, site_number. If payment_info supplied, calls `_save_bank_details()` and merges result.

**get_site**: receives CfsAccountModel, gets access_token, sends HTTP GET to `{CFS_BASE_URL}/cfs/parties/{party}/accs/{account}/sites/{site}/` with Bearer token, returns JSON response.

**update_site_receipt_method**: receives CfsAccountModel and receipt_method string, sends HTTP PUT (via is_put=True) to same site URL with payload `{'receipt_method': receipt_method}`, returns JSON response.

structured.condensed:
Calls the CFS (payment system) API to save and update bank details, retrieve invoices, apply or unapply invoices to receipts, reverse receipts, and create account invoices. All methods obtain OAuth tokens (PayBC or FAS credential variants) and make HTTP requests to CFS endpoints constructed from configured base URL and account identifiers (party, account, site numbers).

Entry points: `_save_bank_details` (classmethod, no check shown), `get_invoice` (classmethod, no check shown), `reverse_rs_receipt_in_cfs` (classmethod, no check shown), `apply_receipt` (classmethod, no check shown), `unapply_receipt` (classmethod, no check shown), `update_bank_details` (classmethod, no check shown), `get_token` (staticmethod, no check shown), `create_account_invoice` (classmethod, no check shown).

Main flows: `_save_bank_details` sanitizes bank account name (removes non-alphanumeric), zero-pads bank and branch numbers, POST to `/cfs/parties/{party_number}/accs/{account_number}/sites/{site_number}/payment/`, returns extracted payment_instrument_number. `get_invoice` GET from CFS invoice endpoint. `reverse_rs_receipt_in_cfs` POST reversal reason (CFS_NSF_REVERSAL_REASON or CFS_PAYMENT_REVERSAL_REASON based on operation type) and comment. `apply_receipt`/`unapply_receipt` delegate to `_modify_rs_receipt_in_cfs`. `_modify_rs_receipt_in_cfs` POST with verb ('apply'/'unapply') in URL and invoice_number. `update_bank_details` wraps `_save_bank_details` with name override. `get_token` matches PaymentSystem enum, encodes client credentials in Base64 Authorization header, POST form data 'grant_type=client_credentials' to `/oauth/token`. `create_account_invoice` builds invoice payload with CFS_BATCH_SOURCE, CFS_CUST_TRX_TYPE, CFS_TERM_NAME constants and current timestamp, POST to CFS sites/invs endpoint.

All outbound calls use OAuthService.post or CFSService methods with bearer or basic auth tokens; no retry, failure handling, or transactional guarantees shown. Bank account name truncated to 30 characters. This chunk shows no entry-point permission checks.

structured.condensed:
Builds invoice line items for the CFS system, grouping them by distribution code and adding up amounts where codes match; also adjusts invoices by creating reversal or adjustment records in CFS, and creates receipt records for payments.

Entry points: `build_lines` (classmethod, called from invoice creation, no check shown); `reverse_invoice` (staticmethod, no check shown); `add_nsf_adjustment` (classmethod, no check shown); `adjust_invoice` (classmethod, no check shown); `create_cfs_receipt` (staticmethod, no check shown).

Inbound: `build_lines` takes list of PaymentLineItemModel with total, service_fees, description, fee_distribution_id; `reverse_invoice` takes invoice number string; `add_nsf_adjustment` takes CfsAccountModel, invoice number, amount float; `adjust_invoice` takes CfsAccountModel, invoice number, optional amount and adjustment_lines; `create_cfs_receipt` takes CfsAccountModel, receipt fields, payment method, optional access token.

Outbound: `build_lines` returns list of line dicts with line_number, line_type (CFS_LINE_TYPE), description, unit_price (negated if negate=True), quantity=1, and distribution array containing dist_line_number, amount, account (formatted as `client.responsibility_centre.service_line.stob.project_code.000000.0000`); reversal POSTs to CFS endpoint `/cfs/parties/invs/{inv_number}/creditbalance/` with empty payload; NSF adjustment POSTs to `/cfs/parties/{cfs_party}/accs/{cfs_account}/sites/{cfs_site}/invs/{inv_number}/adjs/` with comment "Non sufficient funds charge for rejected PAD Payment" and activity_name "BC Registries - NSF Charge"; `adjust_invoice` POSTs to same endpoint with comment "Invoice cancellation"; `create_cfs_receipt` POSTs to `/cfs/parties/{cfs_party}/accs/{cfs_account}/sites/{cfs_site}/rcpts/` with receipt_number, receipt_date, receipt_amount, payment_method (mapped CFS_DRAWDOWN_BALANCE for drawdown; CFS_CASH_RCPT for cash/cheque; CFS_RCPT_EFT_WIRE otherwise), comments=''.

All CFS calls fetch bearer token via CFSService.get_token(), send Content-Type: application/json. Lines are grouped by distribution_code_id in a map; subsequent items with same ID accumulate into unit_price and distribution amount. No duplicate guard for line items. GOTCHA: `adjust_invoice` comment notes CFS does not return line numbers so rebuilt lines may not match originals. GOTCHA: `build_lines` uses list comprehension to find distribution code—will crash if fee_distribution_id has no match in distribution_codes list.

Fetches receipt and credit memo (CMS) details from the CFS financial service, creates new credit memos, and adjusts receipt balances to zero by applying refunds or write-offs.

Entry points: `get_receipt(cfs_account, receipt_number)` is a class method that any caller may invoke with no check shown; retrieves and returns receipt details. `get_cms(cfs_account, cms_number)` retrieves and returns credit memo details; no check shown. `create_cms(line_items, cfs_account)` creates a credit memo; no check shown. `adjust_receipt_to_zero(cfs_account, receipt_number, is_refund=False)` queries a receipt's `unapplied_amount`, and if positive, posts an adjustment with `activity_name` set to "Refund Adjustment FAS" or "Write-off Adjustment FAS" based on `is_refund`, then re-queries to confirm; no check shown.

Flow: Each method obtains an access token via `CFSService.get_token()`, constructs a CFS endpoint URL using `CFS_BASE_URL` config key and account identifiers (party, account, site), and sends a GET or POST request with BEARER auth. `get_receipt` and `get_cms` return the JSON response. `create_cms` builds a payload with `batch_source` = `CFS_CM_BATCH_SOURCE`, `cust_trx_type` = `CFS_CMS_TRX_TYPE`, `transaction_date` and `gl_date` set to current time (from `current_local_time()`), empty `comments`, and `lines` from `cls.build_lines(line_items, negate=True)`, then posts and returns JSON.

GOTCHA: `adjust_receipt_to_zero` logs the unapplied amount but does not check the adjustment POST response for success or record whether it failed; a failure in the adjustment call is not caught, logged, or retried.

structured.condensed: Service to manage direct payments to PayBC, a payment gateway. Entry point `get_payment_system_url_for_invoice` (callable by any caller; this chunk shows no check) takes an Invoice and return URL, builds a payment request by assembling transaction date, PayBC reference number, transaction number, invoice total, payment method, revenue distribution, and a hash of the parameters. It returns the PayBC portal URL with encoded parameters. `create_invoice` (callable by any caller; this chunk shows no check) checks `ensure_no_payment_blockers` on the payment account, then returns a static InvoiceReference with a generated transaction number. `update_invoice` does nothing, as direct payments cannot be updated. `get_pay_system_reason_code` parses the response URL; if `trnApproved` equals '1' the payment succeeded, else it looks up the error message text in `PAYBC_TRANSACTION_ERROR_MESSAGE_DICT` to map a reason code, defaulting to 'GENERIC_ERROR'. `get_receipt` (callable by any caller; this chunk shows no check) validates the response hash if `trnApproved` is '1', retrieves the PayBC transaction number from the response or invoice reference, calls PayBC's transaction endpoint with a bearer token to fetch payment status, and returns order ID, date, and amount if status is in `STATUS_PAID`. `process_cfs_refund` (callable by any caller; this chunk shows no check) checks that the invoice status is PAID or UPDATE_REVENUE_ACCOUNT, calls `build_automated_refund_payload`, and POSTs to the PayBC refund endpoint with a bearer token; if the response `approved` field is not 1, raises `BusinessException(Error.DIRECT_PAY_INVALID_RESPONSE)`. HTTPErrors are caught, logged, and re-raised as BusinessException. Helper `_create_revenue_string` queries PaymentLineItemModel by invoice ID, iterates line items, looks up DistributionCodeModel by fee distribution ID, formats GL coding with client, responsibility centre, service line, STOB, project code, and amount, and joins revenue items. Helper `_get_gl_coding` assembles GL account code from distribution code fields with an optional amount suffix. GOTCHA: `process_cfs_refund` does not save payment state before the refund request; if the POST succeeds but a later step fails, no record is persisted. GOTCHA: `get_receipt` validates hash only when `trnApproved` is '1', but an attacker could flip the flag to '0' to bypass validation. GOTCHA: the response hash validation in `get_receipt` uses `urlencode(parsed_args)` after popping `hashValue`, meaning the order of parameters in the URL affects the hash check; if PayBC or the caller changes parameter order, validation fails silently and returns None without logging why.

structured.condensed:
Obtains OAuth tokens from PayBC and executes automated partial refunds by requesting order status, validating refund amounts, matching revenue accounts to distribution codes, and building the refund payload.

Entry points: `get_token()` (instance method, no check shown), `_get_refund_token()` (classmethod, no check shown), `query_order_status(invoice, inv_status)` (classmethod, no check shown), `build_automated_refund_payload(invoice, refund_partial)` (classmethod, no check shown).

Flow: `get_token()` encodes `PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_CLIENT_ID` and `PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_CLIENT_SECRET` in base64, POSTs to `PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_BASE_URL/oauth/token` with grant_type=client_credentials and BASIC auth, returns token response. `_get_refund_token()` encodes same credentials, GETs from `PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_CC_REFUND_BASE_URL/paybc-service/oauth/token/` with BASIC auth under header `Basic-Token`, returns token response. `query_order_status()` calls `get_token()`, GETs invoice status from PayBC at `PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_BASE_URL/paybc/payment/{PAYBC_DIRECT_PAY_REF_NUMBER}/{invoice_number}` with Bearer token, structures response as OrderStatus. `build_automated_refund_payload()` finds Receipt and InvoiceReference, builds payload with orderNumber, pbcRefNumber, txnAmount, txnNumber; if refund_partial provided, calls `_build_refund_revenue_lines()` which validates each refund_amount against PaymentLineItem's service_fees or total, determines revenue_account via DistributionCode, appends RefundLineRequest; then calls `query_order_status()`, validates no prior refund via postedrefundamount and refundedamount, matches each refund line's revenue_account to PayBC invoice revenue by revenueaccount (excluding linenumber '1' for service fees), validates refund amount against revenue_match.revenueamount, updates payload with refundRevenue lines and adjusted txnAmount.

Decisions: `_validate_refund_amount()` raises Error.INVALID_REQUEST if refund_amount > max_amount. `_build_refund_revenue_lines()` raises if PaymentLineItem not found or refund_amount < 0; raises if is_service_fee and no fee_distribution.service_fee_distribution_code_id exists. `_build_refund_revenue()` raises if postedrefundamount or refundedamount > 0 (prior refund detected); raises if revenue_match not found (no matching distribution code); skips refund lines with refund_amount == 0.

GOTCHA: no caller check for entry points; refund payload txnAmount is reset to total_refund, discarding original invoice.total when partial refund provided.

Three static methods on a service class that retrieve, create and update distribution codes—the ledger accounts to which fees and disbursements are charged. find_fee_schedules_by_distribution_id retrieves all fee schedules linked to a distribution code by id, returning a list. save_or_update takes a distribution_details dict and optional dist_id: parses startDate and endDate fields (startDate defaults to today UTC), detects whether client, responsibilityCentre, serviceLine, projectCode or serviceFeeDistributionCodeId have changed from the current DAO, and if any changed on an existing distribution, calls InvoiceModel.update_invoices_for_revenue_updates on the dist_id and on all distributions that reference it as their serviceFeeDistributionCodeId. It sets stop_ejv to false, saves the DistributionCode DAO, and returns the dumped schema. create_link iterates a fee_schedules list, creates DistributionCodeLinkModel objects linking each feeScheduleId to the dist_id, and bulk-saves them. asdict returns the DAO as a dumped dict.

GOTCHA: save_or_update sets stop_ejv to false before every save unconditionally, overwriting any prior state.

Service to manage EJV Payments for government accounts through the CGI payment system.

Entry points: `create_invoice(payment_account, line_items, invoice)` callable by any caller (no check shown); `complete_post_invoice(invoice, invoice_reference)` callable by any caller (no check shown); `process_cfs_refund(invoice, payment_account, refund_partial)` callable by any caller (no check shown).

`create_invoice` flow: ensures no payment blockers on the account; if account is not billable, creates an InvoiceReference with a generated transaction number and returns it; otherwise returns None. Decision: if `payment_account.billable` is false, creates and returns an InvoiceReference; else returns None.

`complete_post_invoice` flow: checks if invoice_reference exists and its status_code equals `InvoiceReferenceStatus.ACTIVE.value`; if true, calls `complete_payment(invoice, invoice_reference)`. Then publishes a message via `_release_payment(invoice)`.

`process_cfs_refund` flow: if account is not billable, returns `InvoiceStatus.REFUNDED.value`. If `invoice.invoice_status_code` equals `InvoiceStatus.APPROVED.value`: if an active invoice reference exists, returns `InvoiceStatus.REFUND_REQUESTED.value`; else returns `InvoiceStatus.CANCELLED.value`. Otherwise returns `InvoiceStatus.REFUND_REQUESTED.value`.

Return codes: `REFUNDED`, `REFUND_REQUESTED`, `CANCELLED` as strings.

GOTCHA: `create_invoice` shows no permission check. GOTCHA: `complete_post_invoice` does not record or handle failures from `complete_payment` or `_release_payment`.

structured.condensed: Service to manage Fee related operations. Holds fee schedule properties (fee_schedule_id, filing_type_code, corp_type_code, fee_code, fee dates, amounts) and delegates storage to FeeScheduleModel DAO via a lazy-loaded _dao property. Properties sync bidirectionally with the DAO: setting a property syncs to DAO, setting _dao pulls all properties from it. Computes total fees as fee_amount + pst + gst + priority_fee + future_effective_fee + service_fees, and total_excluding_service_fees without service_fees. The quantity setter multiplies fee_amount by quantity if quantity > 1. The fee_amount setter records waived_fee_amount as the original amount plus priority_fee and future_effective_fee if fee_amount is set to 0 and not variable. asdict() exports fields to a dict with floats and nested tax object. save() persists the DAO. find_by_corp_type_and_filing_type() (classmethod, requires user_context decorator; raises BusinessException if corp_type and filing_type_code both missing or no matching fee_schedule_dao found) fetches FeeScheduleModel by corp type, filing type, and valid_date; sets quantity; checks AccountFeeModel for apply_filing_fees override (defaults true); zeros fee_amount and waived_fee_amount if apply_filing_fees is false; calculates service_fees via FeeSchedule.calculate_service_fees(); applies priority_fee and future_effective_fee if requested and apply_filing_fees is true; zeros all fees if waive_fees is true. GOTCHA: fee_amount setter only sets waived_fee_amount if fee_amount==0 and not variable, so waived amounts from other paths are not tracked.

Structured logging for Knative: emits JSON log entries to stdout with severity, message, caller context, and optional Google Cloud trace correlation.

Entry point `structured_log(request, severity, message)` callable by any code; this chunk shows no check. Reads `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` environment variable and `X-Cloud-Trace-Context` request header (when both present, extracts trace ID and nests log under Google Cloud trace). Introspects stack to capture caller's module name and function name via `inspect.stack()` and `inspect.getmodule()`. Outputs JSON object with `severity`, `message`, `component` (caller identity as `module.function`), and optional `logging.googleapis.com/trace` field. No conditional logic on message content; trace correlation depends solely on environment variable and header presence.

structured.condensed: Manages internal payments for zero-dollar or staff transactions in a payment system. Receives a payment account, line items, and invoice. If a routing slip number is present, validates it, decrements its remaining amount, and marks it complete if depleted; otherwise creates an invoice reference with a generated transaction number and sets invoice status to CREATED. Returns invoice reference or static receipt (invoice number, current UTC time, total). On post-invoice completion, marks payment complete and releases it if not already approved. On refund request, validates routing slip exists and is active or complete, finds the associated payment, marks it refunded, restores routing slip remaining amount, reverts routing slip to active if it was complete, and sets invoice status to REFUND_REQUESTED. Validates routing slip: raises error if legacy mode is off and slip is absent, if slip is NSF with zero balance, if slip is not in active/linked/NSF/correction status, if slip is linked to a parent, or if remaining amount is insufficient. GOTCHA: process_cfs_refund checks invoice.total == 0 twice with identical outcomes; saves changes to payment and routing slip via flush (non-transactional), no retry on failure.

Provides static methods to query and manipulate invoices for a billing system, and generates PDF receipts.

**Entry points (all static, no check shown):**
- `find_invoices_for_payment(payment_id, reference_status=ACTIVE)` – returns List[Invoice] by querying InvoiceModel.find_invoices_for_payment with payment_id and reference_status.
- `find_invoices(business_identifier)` – returns Dict with 'invoices' key containing list, queries InvoiceModel.find_by_business_identifier, transforms each DAO to Invoice.asdict().
- `has_overdue_invoices(payment_account_id)` – returns bool, queries InvoiceModel where invoice_status_code==OVERDUE and payment_account_id match.
- `create_invoice_pdf(identifier, **kwargs)` decorated with @user_context – decorated method receiving user in kwargs; loads InvoiceModel by identifier, raises BusinessException(Error.INVALID_INVOICE_ID) if not found; fetches PaymentAccountModel and CfsAccountModel; calls OAuthService.get to AUTH_API_ENDPOINT/orgs/{auth_account_id} and /orgs/{auth_account_id}/contacts with user.bearer_token (AuthHeaderType.BEARER, ContentType.JSON); extracts first contact or empty dict; uses invoice_dao.references[0].invoice_number or generate_transaction_number(invoice_dao.id); builds filing_types list from payment_line_items with folioNumber, description, businessIdentifier (empty if starts with 'T'), createdOn, filingTypeCode, fee, gst, serviceFees; calls OAuthService.post to REPORT_API_BASE_URL with bearer token, ContentType.JSON, template dict (templateName='invoice', reportName=invoice_number, templateVars, populatePageNumber=True); returns (pdf_response, invoice_number).
- `_check_for_auth(dao, one_of_roles=ALL_ALLOWED_ROLES)` – calls check_auth(dao.business_identifier, one_of_roles).
- `_add_dynamic_fields(invoice, calculate_dynamic_fields=False)` – if calculate_dynamic_fields: sets is_payment_action_required=True when status_code==CREATED and payment_method in (DIRECT_PAY, CC, ONLINE_BANKING); if payment_method==ONLINE_BANKING, calls CodeService.find_code_value_by_type_and_code(CORP_TYPE, corp_type_code), sets is_online_banking_allowed=False if any line_item.future_effective_fees!=0, returns modified invoice dict.

GOTCHA: create_invoice_pdf shows no authorization check, only @user_context decorator (real check may be elsewhere). GOTCHA: org_contact_response fallback to empty dict means contact fields may be null. GOTCHA: invoice_dao.references may be empty (generates fallback number).

Service to manage Non-Sufficient Funds (NSF) records tied to invoices.

Entries: `save_non_sufficient_funds(invoice_id, invoice_number, cfs_account, description)` creates an NSF record for a given invoice; `exists_for_invoice_number(invoice_number)` checks if NSF exists; `find_all_non_sufficient_funds_invoices(account_id)` retrieves all NSF invoices for an account with totals; `create_non_sufficient_funds_statement_pdf(account_id, **kwargs)` generates a PDF statement. The PDF method requires `user` in kwargs with `bearer_token` and is decorated with `@user_context`; this chunk shows no permission check.

Flow: `save_non_sufficient_funds` stores description, invoice_id, invoice_number, and cfs_account to the NonSufficientFunds table and returns the saved DAO wrapped as dict. `find_all_non_sufficient_funds_invoices` queries invoices linked to NSF records where invoice_status_code ≠ PAID, computes `amount_remaining` (total - paid), finds max NSF line item amount where description equals `ReverseOperation.NSF.value`, sums these across invoices, and returns dict with total, invoices list, statements list, total_amount, total_amount_remaining, nsf_amount (all as floats). `create_non_sufficient_funds_statement_pdf` fetches the NSF invoice data, retrieves the payment account, finds its latest CFS account with PaymentMethod.PAD, retrieves account details via OAuth, extracts suspendedOn date if present, builds template vars including businessName (fallback to createdBy), amounts, and invoices, then POSTs to report API with template name 'non_sufficient_funds' and template vars, returning PDF response and report name.

Saves: NonSufficientFunds row in save_non_sufficient_funds before returning. No retry, no failure recording shown.

GOTCHA: `create_non_sufficient_funds_statement_pdf` accesses `invoice['invoices'][0]['id']` without length check, will fail if invoices list is empty.

Service to invoke REST endpoints using OAuth 2.0 with token-based authentication.

Entry points: two static methods callable by any code.

`post()`: sends POST or PUT (if `is_put=True`) to `endpoint` with data serialized to JSON (via DecimalEncoder) or passed as-is depending on `content_type`. Constructs Authorization header using `token` formatted by `auth_header_type.value`, adds Content-Type header, merges `additional_headers` if provided, then sends with timeout from config key `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`. Logs endpoint, headers (with Authorization redacted), and data before send. Logs response headers and JSON response (with access_token redacted). On connection error or timeout, wraps in ServiceUnavailableException and raises. On HTTPError: if status >= 500, wraps in ServiceUnavailableException and raises; otherwise raises as-is if `raise_for_error=True`, else returns response. Always logs response in finally block. Returns response object.

`get()`: sends GET to `endpoint` with same Authorization and Content-Type headers as post. Mounts RETRY_ADAPTER (max_retries=5, backoff_factor=1, status_forcelist=[404]) if `retry_on_failure=True`. On connection error or timeout, wraps in ServiceUnavailableException and raises. On HTTPError: if status >= 500, wraps in ServiceUnavailableException and raises; if status == 404 and `return_none_if_404=True`, returns None; otherwise raises. Always logs response in finally block. Returns response or None.

Authorization header name defaults to 'Authorization' but is customizable via `auth_header_name` parameter.

GOTCHA: no duplicate guard, no permission check shown; retry logic only active when explicitly requested via `retry_on_failure=True`; 404 responses are not logged at info level in get().

structured.condensed: Integrates invoicing and payments with PayBC (British Columbia's payment system). Entry points: `get_payment_system_url_for_invoice` and `get_payment_system_url_for_payment` return a PayBC portal URL built from invoice number, reference number, and a URL-encoded redirect URI. `create_account` calls `create_cfs_account` with identifier and contact info, saves returned account number, site number, and party number to CfsAccountModel, sets status ACTIVE and payment method CC. `create_invoice` calls `create_account_invoice` with line item models and returns an InvoiceReference with invoice number and pbc_ref_number from the response. `update_invoice` reverses the existing invoice then creates a new one with reference count in the invoice number. `cancel_invoice` reverses an invoice to zero. `get_receipt` (called with pay response URL and invoice reference): obtains bearer token from `CFSService.get_token()`, queries CFS receipt endpoint; if no receipt_number in URL, iterates all receipts to find one matching the invoice number, else uses receipt_number from URL; returns receipt number, parsed receipt date, and amount applied. `process_cfs_refund` delegates to parent `_refund_and_create_credit_memo`. `get_payment_system_code` returns PAYBC. `get_payment_method_code` returns CC. Helper `_build_payment_url` constructs URL from PAYBC_PORTAL_URL config, invoice and reference numbers, and redirect URI. Helper `_get_receipt_by_number` fetches receipt details. Helper `get_non_null_value` returns default if value is null or empty. This chunk shows no permission checks on entry points. GOTCHA: `get_receipt` iterates all receipts if receipt_number is absent, accumulating amount as Decimal but returning float—may lose precision.

structured.condensed: Creates or retrieves a payment record for an account, handling retry payments and invoice consolidation. Intake: account ID, flags for retry and whether to pay outstanding balance or all invoice statuses. Outflow: Payment object. Main flow: (1) If retry payment, fetch failed payments; if paying outstanding balance with no prior failures, consolidate invoices. (2) If exactly one failure or a partial failure exists, check for stale CREATED payment by invoice number—reuse if found, else create new payment for the shortfall amount. (3) If multiple failures without a partial, consolidate them. (4) Log and return payment. Decisions: (A) is_retry_payment and pay_outstanding_balance with no failed payments → call _consolidate_invoices_and_pay; (B) can_consolidate_invoice true → call _consolidate_payments; (C) stale_payments found → reuse Payment from stale_payments[0]; (D) failed_payment.payment_status_code == FAILED → create new Payment for shortfall; (E) else → populate from failed_payment. Helper _consolidate_invoices_and_pay: finds outstanding invoices, reverses existing consolidated invoices in CFS via credit memo, creates new consolidated invoice in CFS, updates invoice references (cancel ACTIVE, add new ACTIVE with is_consolidated=true), creates Payment with new invoice_number. Helper create_consolidated_invoices_payment: consolidates multiple invoices, checks CFS for existing invoice by number, creates if missing, updates invoice references, creates Payment. No entry-point checks shown. No retry or failure recording shown beyond debug log. GOTCHA: Multiple stale CREATED payments can exist (race condition noted in comment) but only first is used.

structured.condensed: Consolidates failed payments by reversing their invoices in CFS, combining their line items, creating a new consolidated invoice, and marking originals as deleted or consolidated. Entry points: `_consolidate_payments` (class method, called internally to handle a list of failed payments for an auth account; no check shown) and `create_payment_receipt` (static method decorated with `@user_context`, creates a payment receipt in response to a credit request; no check shown). Inputs: auth account ID, failed payments list, or credit request dict with paymentMethod, paymentDate, paidAmount. Flow: (1) fetch PaymentAccount and CfsAccount by auth account and payment method; (2) for each failed payment, reverse its invoice via CFSService and collect all related invoices; (3) create consolidated invoices and payment; (4) update each failed payment with consolidated invoice number and mark as DELETED if already CREATED; (5) commit; or for receipt: create Payment record, generate receipt number, call CFSService.create_cfs_receipt, set payment fields and status to COMPLETED, save. Outputs: Payment object. Calls: PaymentAccountModel.find_by_auth_account_id, CfsAccountModel.find_effective_by_payment_method, CFSService.reverse_invoice (with inv_number), InvoiceModel.find_invoices_for_payment, create_consolidated_invoices_payment, CFSService.create_cfs_receipt (with cfs_account, rcpt_number, rcpt_date, amount, payment_method), generate_receipt_number, parser.parse. Saves before commit: failed_payment.cons_inv_number, failed_payment.payment_status_code. GOTCHA: no duplicate guard when consolidating; PAD-only consolidation but no EFT validation stops users switching payment methods mid-consolidation; no explicit failure handling shown for CFS calls or commit.

structured.condensed: Service wrapper for PaymentAccountModel that manages payment account state, including related CFS account details. Entry points: `create()` class method creates new payment account (fails if auth_account_id already exists via PaymentAccountModel.find_by_auth_account_id check), then persists default statement frequency, checks/updates statement notifications, publishes mailer event. Main flow: `_dao` property lazily initializes PaymentAccountModel and on assignment loads effective CfsAccountModel by payment_account.id and payment_method, populating cfs_account, cfs_party, cfs_site, bank numbers, cfs_account_id, and status fields. `__setattr__` proxies attribute writes to `_dao` when attributes exist there, else to object itself. `_save_account()` updates payment_account from account_request dict, checks for payment method changes via `_check_and_handle_payment_method()` (raises EFT_PAYMENT_ACTION_UNSUPPORTED if changing from EFT with flag enable-payment-change-from-eft on; raises EFT_SHORT_NAME_OUTSTANDING_BALANCE if changing from EFT with outstanding balance > 0), generates interim statement, calls `_check_and_update_statement_settings()` (sets statement frequency to MONTHLY for EFT, updates via StatementSettings.update_statement_settings), and `_check_and_update_statement_notifications()` (enables notifications for EFT, auto-populates StatementRecipient records with org admins if none exist via get_account_admin_users call). GOTCHA: `create()` saves payment_account then publishes mailer event after—if event publish fails, account persists. GOTCHA: no transactional guarantee across `_persist_default_statement_frequency()`, statement notifications, and account save.

structured.condensed:
Manages payment account setup and configuration for auth accounts: creates or updates CFS accounts in payment systems (PayBC, CGI), handles PAD (Pre-Authorized Debit) activation timing with a 3-day wait, manages distribution codes for GOVM accounts, and persists account fees and statement frequency settings.

Entry points: `_handle_payment_details` (called to initialize account for a payment system—this chunk shows no check), `save_account_fees`, `get_account_fees`, `save_account_fee`, `delete_account_fees`, `update`, `find_account`, `find_by_auth_account_id`.

Incoming: `PaymentDetails` with nested `payment_account` (id, auth_account_id, payment_method, name, pad_activation_date), `pay_system` (PayBC or CGI), `account_request` (contactInfo, paymentInfo), `payment_info` (revenueAccount), `is_sandbox` flag, `previous_payment` method. Fee requests carry `accountFees` array with per-item `applyFilingFees`, `serviceFeeCode`, `product`.

Flow: For PayBC, look up or create `CfsAccountModel`, flush to DB, then call `_update_pad_activation_date`—if PAD and sandbox, set status ACTIVE and date to now; if PAD and live, compute effective method and activation date (3-day offset if first time, else reuse existing date or collapse to previous method). For CGI (GOVM), end-date any active distribution code to yesterday, upsert new one from `revenueAccount`. For other systems, if feature flag `multiple-payment-methods` is false, find pending PAD account and mark it INACTIVE to block auto-switch. Fee methods: find or create `AccountFeeModel` per product, set `apply_filing_fees`, `service_fee_code`, save.

Decisions: `details.pay_system.get_payment_system_code() == PaymentSystem.PAYBC.value` → create or update CfsAccount; `== PaymentSystem.CGI.value` → manage distribution codes; else → handle PAD deactivation. `is_pad and is_sandbox` → set ACTIVE; `is_pad and not sandbox` → defer by 3 days or reuse. `is_first_time_pad` → calculate new date; `is_previous_pad_activated` → reuse PAD; else → revert to previous method.

Outgoing: calls `CfsAccountModel.find_effective_by_payment_method`, `details.pay_system.create_account` (sends auth_account_id, contactInfo, paymentInfo, payment_method; receives CfsAccountModel or None), `pay_system.update_account` (sends name, cfs_account, payment_info), `DistributionCode.find_active_by_account_id`, `DistributionCode.save_or_update` (receives revenue_account dict with accountId, name), `CfsAccountModel.flush()` mid-transaction, `flags.is_on` (reads `multiple-payment-methods` feature flag), `StatementSettingsModel.save()`, `PaymentAccountModel.find_by_auth_account_id`, `AccountFeeModel.find_by_account_id_and_product`, `AccountFeeModel.find_by_account_id`.

State saved early: `CfsAccountModel.flush()` after create (before subsequent call to `_update_pad_activation_date` can fail); `DistributionCode.save()` and `DistributionCode.save_or_update()` commit before others. No explicit retry or failure recording shown; exception `ServiceUnavailableException` caught and re-raised in `update()`.

GOTCHA: `details.pay_system.create_account()` has `pylint:disable=assignment-from-none` comment—may return None and will not error if CfsAccount creation fails external to this code. GOTCHA: `CfsAccountModel.flush()` is mid-transaction and does not commit; later failure leaves incomplete state. GOTCHA: PAD activation logic is complex and mutates `details.payment_account.pad_activation_date` and `payment_method` in-place during `_update_pad_activation_date`, modifying input object. GOTCHA: fee delete is a list comprehension that silently swallows any individual delete errors.

structured.condensed: Retrieves, searches and serializes payment accounts for a financial system. Entry points: `find_by_id(account_id)` finds a single account by ID with no check shown; `search_eft_accounts(search_text)` finds up to 20 EFT accounts in ACTIVE or PENDING status matching auth_account_id, name or branch_name, ordered by exact match then ID descending, requires no check shown; `asdict(**kwargs)` returns account as dict, decorated with `@user_context`, calls role-based visibility checks—`user.is_system()` or `user.can_view_bank_info()` for CFS details, `user.can_view_bank_account_number()` for unmasked bank account—and includes PAD-specific future state if `_is_pad_in_pending_activation()` returns true, includes EJV revenue account if payment_method is EJV, includes account fees if any exist; `publish_account_mailer_event_on_creation()` publishes to queue if payment_method is PAD; `_calculate_activation_date()` rounds current local time plus PAD_CONFIRMATION_PERIOD_IN_DAYS to day start then converts to UTC. Flow: `_is_pad_in_pending_activation()` checks if pad_activation_date is in future and finds CfsAccountModel with PAD payment method in PENDING or PENDING_PAD_ACTIVATION status. `_publish_queue_message(payload, message_type)` calls `gcp_queue_publisher.publish_to_queue()` with QueueMessage; exceptions are logged and captured via Sentry, not retried or re-raised. `create_account_event_payload(event_type, receipt_info, include_pay_info)` builds dict with accountId, accountName, and conditional fields: NSF_UNLOCK_ACCOUNT adds invoice details; PAD_ACCOUNT_CREATE adds padTosAcceptedBy; include_pay_info adds bank details with masked account number and formatted pad_activation_date. GOTCHA: exception in `_publish_queue_message` is swallowed—queued messages may silently fail. GOTCHA: `asdict` shows no caller identity check beyond user role—any authenticated user with appropriate role gets bank details.

structured.condensed:
Unlocks frozen payment accounts due to NSF or overdue invoices, reverses original invoices when needed, and publishes an account event to a queue for downstream notification.

Entry points: `unlock_frozen_accounts(payment_id, payment_account_id, invoice_number)` (staticmethod, no check shown), `delete_account(auth_account_id)` (classmethod, no check shown), `enable_eft(auth_account_id)` (classmethod, no check shown).

**unlock_frozen_accounts**: Retrieves PaymentAccountModel by payment_account_id. Decision: if account has_nsf_invoices, logs unlock, finds PAD CfsAccountModel, calls CFSService.update_site_receipt_method with receipt_method=RECEIPT_METHOD_PAD_DAILY, sets has_nsf_invoices to None, saves both pay_account and cfs_account with status ACTIVE; elif has_overdue_invoices, reverses each original invoice via InvoiceReferenceModel.find_non_consolidated_invoice_numbers (silently logs exceptions without re-raising), sets has_overdue_invoices to None, saves pay_account. Only if unlocked=True: retrieves ReceiptService.get_nsf_receipt_details(payment_id), finds PaymentAccount service by payment_account_id, creates payload via create_account_event_payload(QueueMessageTypes.NSF_UNLOCK_ACCOUNT.value, receipt_info=receipt_info), publishes to gcp_queue_publisher.publish_to_queue with source=QueueSources.PAY_API.value, message_type=QueueMessageTypes.NSF_UNLOCK_ACCOUNT.value, topic=AUTH_EVENT_TOPIC config key (logs and captures exception on failure, does not retry or re-raise).

**delete_account**: Retrieves PaymentAccountModel by auth_account_id. Three decision gates with BusinessException raised: if credit > 0 (Error.OUTSTANDING_CREDIT); if CfsAccountModel (PAD) status equals CfsAccountStatus.FREEZE.value (Error.FROZEN_ACCOUNT); if InvoiceModel.find_outstanding_invoices_for_account within get_outstanding_txns_from_date() (Error.TRANSACTIONS_IN_PROGRESS). Then: if CfsAccountModel exists and status not already INACTIVE, sets status to INACTIVE, and if payment_method=PAD and status in [ACTIVE, PENDING_PAD_ACTIVATION], calls CFSService.update_site_receipt_method with receipt_method=RECEIPT_METHOD_PAD_STOP, saves. For all CfsAccountModels by pay_account.id, sets status=INACTIVE and saves. If statement_notification_enabled is True, sets False and saves.

**enable_eft**: Retrieves PaymentAccountModel by auth_account_id. If eft_enable not already True, sets eft_enable=True, saves, finds PaymentAccount service, creates payload via create_account_event_payload(QueueMessageTypes.EFT_AVAILABLE_NOTIFICATION.value), calls _publish_queue_message(payload, QueueMessageTypes.EFT_AVAILABLE_NOTIFICATION.value).

GOTCHA: Invoice reversal exceptions caught and logged but not re-raised; partial updates occur before queue publish fails. GOTCHA: Queue publish exceptions caught and logged but not re-raised or retried.

structured.condensed: Service class to manage payment line item records—which itemise the filing fees, priority fees, future effective fees, and tax components of an invoice. Entry point: static `create(invoice_id, fee, **kwargs)` method checks that only users with Role.STAFF can waive fees (raises BusinessException(Error.FEE_OVERRIDE_NOT_ALLOWED) otherwise); accepts a FeeSchedule and copies its attributes (fee_amount, priority_fee, future_effective_fee, gst, pst, quantity, waived_fee_amount, service_fees, description, fee_schedule_id) to the line item, calculates total as fee.total_excluding_service_fees, sets line_item_status_code to LineItemStatus.ACTIVE.value, and if total or service_fees exceed zero, looks up the active distribution code for that fee_schedule_id and stores its distribution_code_id; if waived fees exist and user is STAFF, records user.user_name in waived_by field; calls flush() to save to database and return a new PaymentLineItem wrapping the saved DAO. Property accessor `find_by_id(line_id)` retrieves a PaymentLineItemModel from database and wraps it. Class wraps a PaymentLineItemModel DAO via lazy-loaded _dao property; all instance properties (id, invoice_id, filing_fees, fee_schedule_id, priority_fees, future_effective_fees, description, gst, pst, total, quantity, line_item_status_code, waived_fees, waived_by, fee_distribution_id, service_fees) sync bidirectionally with DAO on get and set. Public method flush() writes to database. GOTCHA: create() checks Role.STAFF but this chunk shows no check that user context was actually populated by the @user_context decorator; code could fail silently if decorator did not run.

structured.condensed: Service to create and update payment invoices for business filings. Entry point `create_invoice` (classmethod, callable by authorization holder via payment_request and authorization tuple) calculates filing fees, finds or creates a payment account, creates Invoice/PaymentLineItem records in database with flush, sends them to external payment system via PaymentSystemFactory, updates Invoice with payment system references, and returns invoice dict. If payment system creation fails, rolls back Invoice and calls `pay_service.cancel_invoice`. Entry point `update_invoice` (classmethod, callable with invoice_id) either applies account credit to invoice (updating paid amount, credit balance, and calling `pay_service.apply_credit`), or patches payment method from ONLINE_BANKING to CC or DIRECT_PAY—requiring active invoice reference to exist for CC flow, or calling `pay_service.create_invoice` for DIRECT_PAY flow. Checks: EFT method requires 'enable-eft-payment-method' flag on; update_invoice payment patch only allowed if current method is ONLINE_BANKING and new method is CC or DIRECT_PAY. GOTCHA: broad Exception catch in create_invoice swallows errors after logging; rollback only occurs if invoice object exists.
