structured.condensed: Deletes an invoice and its payment records in a payment system. The public method `accept_delete` checks that the caller has EDIT_ROLE, marks the invoice status as DELETE_ACCEPTED, then spawns a thread calling `delete_invoice` asynchronously. The `delete_invoice` classmethod updates active transactions, fetches the invoice (skip_auth_check=True), creates a payment service from the invoice's payment method, checks if deletion is permitted via _check_if_invoice_can_be_deleted, marks the Payment record status as DELETED and flushes it, calls the payment service's cancel_invoice with the payment account and invoice number, marks the Invoice status as DELETED, marks all PaymentLineItem records as CANCELLED, marks the InvoiceReference status as CANCELLED, and saves the invoice. The deletion eligibility check _check_if_invoice_can_be_deleted is called with both payment and without payment in different code paths. GOTCHA: skip_auth_check=True bypasses authorization on invoice lookup; the only permission check shown is one_of_roles=[EDIT_ROLE] in accept_delete, but delete_invoice itself shows no check when called from the spawned thread. GOTCHA: Payment.flush() is called before invoice.save(), creating a partial update window if the invoice save fails. GOTCHA: Thread spawning is not awaited and no error handling is shown for the spawned delete operation.

structured.condensed: Manages payment transaction state: tracks a transaction's id (uuid), status_code, payment_id, client_system_url, pay_system_url, transaction_start_time, transaction_end_time, and pay_system_reason_code. Entry points: `create_transaction_for_payment(payment_id, request_json)` creates a transaction for an existing payment with status CREATED; `create_transaction_for_invoice(invoice_id, request_json)` creates a transaction for an invoice, first creating a payment if needed. Both check the payment_method_code and validate clientSystemUrl. `create_transaction_for_payment` requires payment.payment_status_code == PaymentStatus.CREATED.value or raises INVALID_PAYMENT_ID; shows no caller check. `create_transaction_for_invoice` requires invoice.id and rejects PaymentMethod.PAD; shows no caller check. Internal flow: `_create_transaction` rejects completed or deleted payments, cancels any existing active transaction with status != CANCELLED, creates a new PaymentTransaction with status_code CREATED, flushes to DB, then builds pay_system_url via PaymentTransaction._build_pay_system_url_for_invoice or _build_pay_system_url_for_payment, and saves again. Properties id, status_code, payment_id, client_system_url, pay_system_url, transaction_start_time, transaction_end_time, pay_system_reason_code sync bidirectionally with PaymentTransactionModel DAO. `asdict()` returns dict via PaymentTransactionSchema. GOTCHA: existing active transaction is cancelled without checking for concurrent requests; transaction state is split between this service and PaymentTransactionModel without transactional guarantee between flush and save.

Builds payment system redirect URLs and processes payment transaction callbacks to update invoice and payment records with receipt details.

Entry points: `_build_pay_system_url_for_invoice(invoice, pay_system_service, transaction_id, pay_return_url)` and `_build_pay_system_url_for_payment(payment, pay_system_service, transaction_id, pay_return_url)` build URLs for redirecting to a payment processor; no check shown. `find_by_id(transaction_id)` retrieves a transaction, raising `BusinessException(Error.INVALID_TRANSACTION_ID)` if missing. `find_active_by_invoice_id(invoice_id)` queries active transaction by invoice. `update_transaction(transaction_id, pay_response_url)` is the main handler processing payment callbacks (credit card, BCOL, internal only; does not support PAD or ONLINE BANKING).

`update_transaction` flow: (1) finds transaction; raises `BusinessException(Error.INVALID_TRANSACTION_ID)` if missing or `BusinessException(Error.INVALID_TRANSACTION)` if already `COMPLETED`; (2) finds payment and account; (3) finds all invoices for that payment; (4) if payment status is `COMPLETED` and transaction status is `EVENT_FAILED`, marks transaction `COMPLETED` and publishes to queue, else raises `BusinessException(Error.COMPLETED_PAYMENT)`; (5) creates pay system service from payment method; (6) calls service to get receipt details, catching `ServiceUnavailableException` to extract status code or catching all other exceptions silently; (7) if receipt received, calls `_update_receipt_details()` to save receipt, mark payment and invoices `COMPLETED`, set paid amounts, and publish to queue for non-PAD/EFT methods, else marks transaction `FAILED`; (8) extracts pay system reason code from response URL if not already set; (9) saves transaction end time and response URL to database; (10) if payment now `COMPLETED`, checks for other failed payments or overdue invoices and calls `PaymentAccount.unlock_frozen_accounts()`.

`_update_receipt_details()` sets payment paid amount and date, transaction status to `COMPLETED`. If paid amount is less than owed amount, logs critical alert and sends Sentry error message. Otherwise sets receipt number and payment status to `COMPLETED`, and for each invoice saves receipt, marks `PAID`, saves payment date, updates invoice reference status to `COMPLETED`, and publishes to queue unless payment method is PAD or EFT.

GOTCHA: no check shown for who may call entry points; broad exception handler swallows errors except `ServiceUnavailableException`; partial update—receipt details saved to database before checking if payment status allows it; paid amount is set before checking if it is less than owed, risking inconsistent state; invoice reference status updated but invoice itself not saved before publishing; pay system reason code extraction skipped if `ServiceUnavailableException` already captured.

structured.condensed: Stores receipt details linked to an invoice, retrieves all payment transactions by invoice ID, and publishes payment status changes to a message queue. Entry point `__save_receipt` (static, no check shown) receives an invoice and receipt details array [number, date, amount]; creates or updates a Receipt record and flushes to database. Entry point `find_by_invoice_id` (static, no check shown) receives invoice_id; queries PaymentTransactionModel, deserializes results into a dict with 'items' array via `PaymentTransaction.populate`, returns that dict. Entry point `publish_status` (static, no check shown) receives transaction_dao and invoice; checks if transaction status is COMPLETED—if so, verifies invoice status is PAID and uses COMPLETED, otherwise logs and returns early; if transaction status is not COMPLETED, uses 'TRANSACTION_FAILED'. Publishes via `gcp_queue_publisher.publish_to_queue` with QueueMessage containing source PAY_API, type PAYMENT, payload from `create_event_payload`, topic from `get_topic_for_corp_type(invoice.corp_type_code)`, and corp_type. On publish exception, logs error and warning, sets transaction_dao.status_code to EVENT_FAILED, but does not re-raise. Entry point `create_event_payload` (static, no check shown) receives invoice and status_code; returns camelized dict of PaymentToken(invoice.id, status_code, invoice.filing_id, invoice.corp_type_code). GOTCHA: `__save_receipt` uses `receipt.id` truthiness check on a potentially unfound record; GOTCHA: exception in `publish_status` caught broadly and swallowed without retry.

structured.condensed:
Service to manage Receipt operations for the payment system.

Entries: `Receipt()` constructor initializes empty service object with internal DAO; `save()` and `flush()` persist current receipt to database via DAO; `find_by_id(receipt_id)` and `find_by_invoice_id_and_receipt_number(invoice_id, receipt_number)` are static finders that load and return Receipt objects wrapping DAO results, no checks shown. `create_receipt(invoice_identifier, filing_data, skip_auth_check)` is static and decorated with `@user_context`, takes bearer token from `kwargs['user']`, calls `Invoice.find_by_id()` with `skip_auth_check` parameter to load invoice; raises `BusinessException(Error.INVALID_REQUEST)` if invoice is not pending (PAD/EJV/EFT with non-PAID status) and has no receipts; calls `InvoiceReference.find_completed_reference_by_invoice_id()` to get invoice number; constructs JSON dict with `templateName='payment_receipt'`, `reportName` from `filing_data['fileName']` or default, and `templateVars` dict; sends via `OAuthService.post()` to REPORT_API_BASE_URL with bearer token and ContentType.JSON; returns PDF response. `get_receipt_details(filing_data, invoice_identifier, skip_auth_check)` static helper builds receipt details dict with invoiceNumber, receiptNumber, filingIdentifier, bcOnlineAccountNumber, paymentMethod, and formatted invoice data; uses `camelcase_dict()` and `get_local_formatted_date()` for formatting. `get_nsf_receipt_details(payment_id)` static helper finds invoices by payment via `Invoice.find_invoices_for_payment(payment_id, COMPLETED)`, selects CC invoice if present, merges non-matching invoices into combined NSF invoice, returns formatted receipt dict.

Properties: `_dao`, `id`, `invoice_id`, `receipt_number`, `receipt_date`, `receipt_amount` are bidirectionally synced between service object and wrapped DAO model.

GOTCHA: `get_receipt_details()` calls `Invoice.find_by_id()` with `skip_auth_check` parameter but this chunk shows no authorization check for who may call `create_receipt()`; a caller elsewhere may check. GOTCHA: `create_receipt()` does not retry `OAuthService.post()` on failure.

structured.condensed:
Generates an interim billing statement when payment account frequency changes, capturing invoices and payment methods up to today, then establishes new statement settings for the transition.

`determine_payment_methods` extracts payment method strings from invoice details matched to a payment account, falling back to existing statement methods or the account's default. `generate_interim_statement` runs when frequency changes: retrieves active statement settings (returns None if missing during account creation); ends the current settings by setting to_date to today; queries invoices and payment accounts within the old frequency period ending today; creates a StatementModel record marking it interim, with notification status determined by account.statement_notification_enabled; bulk-saves StatementInvoicesModel links for each invoice; then creates or updates StatementSettingsModel with new_frequency, from_date set to tomorrow. Payment methods are comma-joined. Statement is saved before invoices are bulk-saved; if bulk save fails, the statement persists unsalvageable.

GOTCHA: `generate_interim_statement` saves the statement and active_settings before bulk-saving statement_invoices; if the bulk insert fails, the statement exists without its invoice links. No error handling or rollback shown.

Entry points: `find_statement_notification_details(auth_account_id)` reads recipients and the account's notification enabled flag by auth_account_id; any caller can invoke with no check shown. `update_statement_notification_details(auth_account_id, notification_details)` updates or creates a PaymentAccount with name and statement_notification_enabled flag, then deletes all StatementRecipientsModel records for that account and bulk-inserts new recipient rows; any caller can invoke with no check shown. The update flow is: look up PaymentAccount by auth_account_id, create if missing, set name and statement_notification_enabled from notification_details dict, save, then if recipients key is not None (empty list means delete all), delete all existing recipients for that account.id and for each recipient dict in the list extract authUserId, firstname, lastname, email and payment_account_id, build StatementRecipientsModel rows and bulk-save them. Instance method `asdict()` serializes self._dao via NotificationSchema.dump(). Properties expose id, auth_user_id, firstname, lastname, email, payment_account_id with getters/setters that mirror to internal _dao object.

Incoming: auth_account_id string; notification_details dict with keys accountName, statementNotificationEnabled, recipients (list of dicts with authUserId, firstname, lastname, email or None). Outgoing: dict with recipients list (schema-dumped) and statement_notification_enabled bool flag. Saved state: PaymentAccount row before recipient delete so a later failure leaves account changes in place. Failures: no retry, no re-raise, no rollback shown.

structured.condensed:
Service class managing statement frequency settings for payment accounts: creates, retrieves, and updates when payment account holders change statement frequency (daily, weekly, monthly).

Entry point: `update_statement_settings(auth_account_id, frequency)` — any caller, no check shown. On first call, creates a StatementSettingsModel record with the frequency; otherwise finds the current active settings (from_date ≤ today and to_date null or ≥ today), handles race condition by marking any unapplied future setting to_date = today, calculates the end date of the longer of current and new frequency, sets current settings' to_date to that end date, saves it, creates and saves a new StatementSettingsModel with from_date = end date + 1 day and the new frequency, returns the new record dumped to dict via schema.

Entry point: `find_by_account_id(auth_account_id)` — any caller, no check shown. Finds the latest (most recent) StatementSettingsModel for the account; if none exists returns None. Otherwise, for each StatementFrequency value, computes the longest frequency between current and that value, gets its end date, and builds a dict with 'frequency' name and 'start_date' = end date + 1 day, collecting these into 'frequencies' list. Returns dict with 'current_frequency' (current settings dumped to dict) and 'frequencies' list.

Entry point: `find_accounts_settings_by_frequency(valid_date, frequency, from_date, to_date)` class method — any caller, no check shown. Queries StatementSettingsModel joined with PaymentAccountModel where from_date ≤ valid_date and (to_date is null or to_date ≥ valid_date) and frequency matches the enum value. If from_date and to_date supplied, also filters to_date == to_date and excludes records where any interim statement exists with matching payment_account_id and from_date ≤ from_date and to_date ≥ to_date. Returns all query results (tuples of StatementSettingsModel and PaymentAccountModel).

GOTCHA: `update_statement_settings` shows no transaction; current and new records are saved separately so a failure between saves leaves inconsistent state. GOTCHA: `find_by_account_id` and `update_statement_settings` receive auth_account_id but show no validation that the caller owns that account.

Entry point: `update_statement_settings(auth_account_id, frequency)` — any caller, no check shown. Entry point: `find_by_account_id(auth_account_id)` — any caller, no check shown. Finds the latest (most recent) StatementSettingsModel for the account; if none exists returns None. Otherwise, for each StatementFrequency value, computes the longest frequency between current and that value, gets its end date, and builds a dict with 'frequency' name and 'start_date' = end date + 1 day, collecting these into 'frequencies' list. Returns dict with 'current_frequency' (current settings dumped to dict) and 'frequencies' list.

Extends the cattrs converter library to serialize and deserialize Decimal, datetime, and Enum types, with optional name-case conversion between camelCase and snake_case for attrs classes.

Entry point: Converter.__init__, called when instantiating this class; this chunk shows no check. Four hooks registered unconditionally: Decimal structures from Any via _structure_decimal (converts to string first, then Decimal); Decimal unstructures to float (or 0 if None); datetime unstructures to ISO format string (or None if None); Enum optionally structures via _to_value if enum_to_value flag is True. Two conditional transformations on attrs classes (has predicate): if camel_to_snake_case, unstructures with snake_case field names and structures expecting camelCase names; if snake_case_to_camel, unstructures to camelCase and structures from camelCase. Case conversion: _to_snake_case uses regex to insert underscores before capitals and lowercases; _to_camel_case splits on underscores, keeps first component, title-cases rest. Utility: remove_nones recursively strips None values and nested dicts from payloads.

GOTCHA: _to_snake_case_structure renames to camelCase when reading input (comment notes this reversal); _unstructure_datetime returns None for None input instead of ISO string.

Defines error codes and their HTTP status responses for a payment system.

The Error enum creates a code, status and optional message for each error condition. The __new__ method adds these attributes to each enum member. get_bcol_error translates BC Online error codes (7, 20, 21, 48, 61, 5) to specific Error enum values; any other code returns BCOL_ERROR. Error codes cover invalid inputs (corporation type, payment method, IDs, transaction), payment states (completed, cancelled, insufficient funds), account issues (closed, revoked, NSF, frozen, incomplete setup), refund constraints, routing slip linking rules, and EFT/FAS payment method validations. Most errors map to HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST; FEE_OVERRIDE_NOT_ALLOWED and INCOMPLETE_ACCOUNT_SETUP map to UNAUTHORIZED; SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE to SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.

When constructed, UserContext extracts username, first name, bearer token, roles (from realm_access.roles), subject, account ID, name, product code, and permissions from g.jwt_oidc_token_info or request headers (Authorization, Account-Id). The decorator user_context adds UserContext as a 'user' kwarg to wrapped functions. Methods: has_role(role_name)—checks if role_name in roles; is_staff()—returns true if Role.STAFF.value in roles; is_system()—returns true if Role.SYSTEM.value in roles; is_sandbox()—returns true if Role.SANDBOX.value in roles; can_view_bank_info()—returns true if any of ['admin', 'view', 'manage_bank_info'] in permission; can_view_bank_account_number()—returns true if any of ['admin', 'view_bank_account_number'] in permission (returns false if permission is None). structured.condensed:
Utility helper module for the payment system. Provides CORS decorator, URL validation, date/time calculations, formatting, and data type conversions.

Entry points: All functions are public utilities; this chunk shows no access checks on any entry point.

Main flow varies by function: `cors_preflight` adds an OPTIONS method to a class returning Allow header and CORS headers; `is_valid_redirect_url` checks if a URL matches config-held valid URLs (exact match or wildcard prefix), with checks disabled if config DISABLE_VALID_REDIRECT_URLS is true; date functions compute week/month boundaries, previous periods, fiscal year (year+1 if month > 3), business days (excluding weekends and BC holidays via Canada library with GOVERNMENT/OPTIONAL/PUBLIC categories plus Easter Monday), and format to local timezone from config LEGISLATIVE_TIMEZONE; `generate_transaction_number` and `generate_receipt_number` format IDs with prefixes from config CFS_INVOICE_PREFIX and CFS_RECEIPT_PREFIX; `get_outstanding_txns_from_date` counts back OUTSTANDING_TRANSACTION_DAYS business days; `mask` replaces characters with 'X' keeping rightmost N chars visible; `parse_url_params` parses query strings; conversions handle None by returning None, `string_to_bool` raises ValueError on invalid input, `get_quantized` rounds to 2 decimals; `get_topic_for_corp_type` maps CorpType NRO to NAMEX_PAY_TOPIC, looks up product via CodeService and maps BUSINESS/BUSINESS_SEARCH to BUSINESS_PAY_TOPIC, STRR to STRR_PAY_TOPIC, returns None otherwise.

Calls out: CodeService.find_code_value_by_type_and_code with Code.CORP_TYPE.value and corp_type, receives product field; reads current_app.config for DISABLE_VALID_REDIRECT_URLS, VALID_REDIRECT_URLS, LEGISLATIVE_TIMEZONE, CFS_INVOICE_PREFIX, CFS_RECEIPT_PREFIX, OUTSTANDING_TRANSACTION_DAYS, NAMEX_PAY_TOPIC, BUSINESS_PAY_TOPIC, STRR_PAY_TOPIC; uses Canada holidays library with BC subdiv and observed=True; uses pytz timezone conversion; uses dpath library get function; uses urllib parse_qsl.

GOTCHA: `is_valid_redirect_url` can be globally disabled via config without warning; `is_holiday` comment notes Easter Monday added despite not official BC STAT; `get_outstanding_txns_from_date` silent infinite loop risk if is_holiday always returns true.
